utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. As indicated, we continue to sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Unless there's anything to be raised -- yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just introduce Ms. Tracey Begley, B-e-g-l-e-y, who has been assisted my team for the last few months. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Welcome, Ms. Begley. Before I forget, I take this opportunity to note that one of our court reporters, Mr. Wayne Bilko, is leaving the Tribunal. Today's the last day. I would like to express our appreciation for his contribution to the Tribunal. Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Good morning, Excellencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I have a problem with a few things. First of all, to establish whether you were given insight into everything, please tell us how you got the material that you analysed, or, rather, on the basis of which you compiled your report. Who gave you this material?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I conducted searches in the databases that are available to the Office of the Prosecutor. The criteria I used to conduct those searches were established by me. I think I briefly addressed that during examination. For example, I would conduct searches on names, names of individuals, on names of locations, on names of military posts, numbers of military units, on names of groups. As you have also seen from the documents, including my report, that military documents have a number and often refer -- in case of orders, they refer to other orders. So, again, these numbers and any reference to other orders would also be used as search criteria. And, of course, I could also rely on the work I had conducted for related cases in the past. The search criteria -- just to finalise my answer, the search criteria were determined by myself only, as I mentioned already, and they were based on my understanding of the guidance, i.e., the direction I had been given as to which topics I was expected to cover in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm concerned as to whether you had insight into all documents. Another thing that is a cause of concern for me: Did you check the authenticity of documents, because there are some forgeries, and we're going to show that here today. Thirdly, your interpretation of a particular document, is it full, is it complete, in relation to everything that happened, in relation to the context, in relation to the document itself, and also in relation to the fine points of linguistics that cannot be translated and were very often mistranslated, at that. Now I would like us to deal with the question of the take-over of power in certain towns. Yesterday, we dealt with the take-over in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic asked a question of the witness, and he should be allowed to answer that, because that's the point of this whole exercise here. He asks the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's the subject I was about to raise. Mr. Theunens -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, there are more than one questions, Dr. Karadzic, so perhaps he could be given a chance to answer each.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I'm well aware that the Office of the Prosecutor does not have all the documents. However, there were no restrictions imposed by anyone on the access I had to the documents that are available in the Office of the Prosecutor. I would also like to add there that in the course of the various trials that have taken place at the ICTY, Defence teams have also introduced documents, and these documents are also available in the databases I consulted to conduct my searches. In relation to authenticity of documents, again a number of these documents, I would say a substantial number of these documents, have also been introduced in other trials and used in those trials. A number of military documents have been shown to military witnesses in order to -- or potential witnesses, I would say, in order to establish their authenticity. Authenticity is a key issue. I would refer -- I would also like to refer to the methodology I applied in relation to see whether the information in the document is credible. There was, I think, a third aspect, but I can't see it anymore on the screen now. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I hope I can assist you, if you would bear with me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The third one is whether your interpretation of a particular document, is it full, is it complete, in relation to everything that happened, in relation to the context, in relation to the document itself, and also in relation to the fine points of linguistics that cannot be translated and were very often mistranslated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. It is my belief that I applied the methodology I have explained in a professional manner, and then it's up to the Trial Chamber to decide whether or not I, indeed, looked at all the documents in the most complete or objective and pragmatic manner possible. As to translation, it is correct, and that has occurred - I've noticed that also several times - that military methodology is not always translated in the correct manner. Now, within the Military Analysis Team, there is -- there are language assistants who have been trained in the use and the translation of military terminology, and I would systematically verify the translation of documents with those language assistants, I mean, translation of military documents, in order to make sure that military terminology in Serbian was translated in the correct manner into English. Now, otherwise -- I mean, most of these documents are very straightforward, so, again, if Mr. Karadzic can identify documents also in relation to the earlier aspects I may have missed, or where I did not provide a full interpretation, or maybe where a translation is incorrect, of course, I'm available to review them now and also reconsider my conclusions, if such a need would arise, on the basis of these additional documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Karadzic, bear that in mind. Your statement is of no value at all during the course of examination. What matters is the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm absolutely aware of that. I just want to make it possible for Mr. Theunens to express himself in the right way, to avoid any kind of confusion. I don't want him to understand that I'm attacking him. I am attacking imprecisions, restraints, limitations in his paper. I am interested in hearing whether he managed to do everything as he had wished. That was my intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you, Mr. Theunens: How was that concept of take-over of power instituted, for example, in the municipalities of North-Western Bosnia-Herzegovina, if I can put it that way?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, when we look at the different municipalities I have discussed in the report, certain patterns can be identified, and these patterns cover at least two aspects, I would say the aspect of preparation, political preparation, and the second aspect is the aspect of implementation. When I talk about political preparation, it means that we see that in those municipalities, in accordance with the instructions of Mr. Karadzic and the SDS, the SDS-led Serb crisis staffs are established. These crisis staffs, I mean, depending on the location, they can declare a state of imminent threat of war. I mean, they have done that in some municipalities. Or they declare mobilisation, or they participate in the establishment or the creation of a local Serb TO, including also, depending on the municipality, appointing commanders on the municipal level, assisting in arming these local Serb TOs. The second aspect, then, the implementation of the take-over, there we see that -- and again it depends a bit on the municipality, but that various forces which I, in maybe a too general manner, identified as Serbs forces, i.e., local Serb TO, sometimes like in Zvornik, also TO of the Republic of Serbia, sometimes also the JNA, elements of the JNA, volunteers from Serbia, sometimes reinforced by local volunteers, as well as also groups that are identified at the time as volunteers, but who actually maintain specific or particular links with the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia; for example, Arkan's Tigers and also individuals or a group who are identified as -- colloquially identified as Red Berets, they participate in the implementation, i.e., in the physical take-over of power, whereby -- I mean, they don't take over power as such, but they occupy what is identified as vital locations in these towns. Okay, in Bijeljina, they first removed or participated in the removal of barricades which had been erected by the Muslim side. And once the take-over has been materialised, it is sometimes, depending on the municipality, accompanied by a removal of non-Serbs. And then, okay, the Bosnian Serb structures of power, I would say, consolidate their power, and, yeah, then the take-over has been accomplished. And this is just a summary of what I've seen in the various municipalities and that is discussed for each analytical conclusion a footnote referring to JNA, or Bosnian Serb MUP, or TO, or VRS document, in Part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's what we read from the documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's my conclusion from the documents, Your Honours, yes. And we can look at the specific municipalities, but these are, in general terms, the patterns I have identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Theunens, that each and every one of those cases is a criminal case, a large-scale criminal case in itself, and that every one of these cases deserves a thorough investigation in order to reach the conclusions that you are referring to, a thorough investigation? Were thorough investigations carried out in each and every one of these cases; for example, with regard to Bijeljina, everything that we discussed yesterday? And if so, who conducted that investigation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not clear in relation to Mr. Karadzic's conclusion that these are criminal cases. I mean, they're obviously, in a number of -- or after doing a number of take-overs, crimes were committed, and when I use the word "crimes," I quoted from documents compiled by members of the police -- of the Bosnian Serb police in those municipalities or at a local level, and these documents are quoted in my report. But my task was not to conduct a criminal investigation. My task was to analyse how the change in authority -- actually, no, I have to rephrase that. I didn't -- my task was not how to analyse how a change in authority took place, but my task was to analyse what happened in these municipalities from the point of view that, okay, on the 12th of May, 1992, at the 16th session of the Assembly of the Bosnian Serbs, the six strategic goals are announced publicly, and, I mean, this is a key event. These six strategic goals, to my knowledge, were never amended during the conflict. So as an analyst, in the framework of the preparation of this report, I wanted to see -- I wanted to analyse when and how these goals were implemented. And my conclusion is that, actually, the implementation of these goals started already prior to their public announcement, and that conclusion is based on my analysis of what I call the take-over operations of municipalities in Northern Bosnia-Herzegovina. And that was the purpose of my analysis, so there was no -- I didn't -- I was not requested or it was not my intention to conduct a criminal investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But what is this expertise, then, Mr. Theunens, if it is not part of a criminal process? What is your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the scope of my report is explained in that particular section called "Scope." My goal is to analyse the role of Mr. Karadzic, as I called it, Supreme Commander over the Bosnian Serb TO and the VRS, whereby I have amended or slightly corrected the use of the term "Supreme commander over the Bosnian Serb TO." There it should be, actually, "the highest political authority over the Bosnian Serb TO." And I conducted that analysis focusing on two aspects. First of all, his de jure and de facto command authority, i.e., the ability to issue order and verify their implementation. And, secondly, his situational awareness, what I called his knowledge and understanding of the situation, capabilities and intention of the Bosnian Serb TO and the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Now we have to move on to specific examples. Can you tell us today, and do you still stand by what you said today, that on the 31st of March and the 1st of April, there was a take-over of power in Bijeljina by someone who was not in power on the 30th of March?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not stated that today, nor yesterday, nor in my report. What I state in my report, that is that based on the documents I reviewed, starting on the night of the 31st of March, and this is footnote 380, military -- military operations, operations or activities that can be qualified as military, in the sense that they involve armed forces, and in this particular case members of the Bosnian Serb TO, which is a newly-established organisation, the Serbian National Guard and the Serbian Volunteer Guard, and these are volunteers/paramilitaries, they start to remove barricades that, according to the source I quoted, "Muslim extremists," had erected. And this continues, then, over the next days. And on the 4th of April, and this is footnote 389, and I apologise repeating all that - I mentioned it yesterday, but apparently the message was not clear - on the 4th of April the JNA 17 Corps Command reports that the town of Bijeljina is controlled by the SDS and Arkan's men, "who do not even allow our armoured unit to reach certain positions in the town."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that that's all what you're saying about Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is what I -- when answering the question of Mr. Karadzic in relation to the take-over and whether there is a change in authority between what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But what did you mean by "take-over"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it means that you remove the -- well, the take-over -- the take-over of physical control, i.e., the taking of the physical control, that is that we see from these documents that the JNA, which in normal conditions would be able to circle it freely in the municipality, as in any other municipality, is now not able to enter Bijeljina, because, as the JNA calls it, it is controlled by the SDS and Arkan's men. So they are physically present on the ground, and they restricted the freedom of movement, not only of the JNA, as we see also from other documents. In addition, "take-over" also implies that other structures of power, I would say political power, start to -- yeah, to -- I mean, they took over -- they took the power from the elected authorities and are now the bodies that are in charge. And we see also, like for other municipalities, that emphasis is laid on the fact that it's not just the Municipality of Zvornik, for example, it's the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik, and these are concepts that did not exist prior to the SDS announcing or calling for the creation of crisis staffs in various municipalities, and, of course, the events during spring 1992, which then culminate in what I call the take-over operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then is your answer to the last question of the accused, i.e., whether there was a take-over of power in Bijeljina, was it yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's my answer, yes, yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us now, who took power over from who? Who won power in Bijeljina and who lost power in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered that question several times. I will do it again. It is that the regular -- I mean, the elected authorities in Bijeljina who would respond to the -- through the various levels of civilian authority and administration to the authorities -- political authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, they are replaced by structures that have been created by the Bosnian Serbs. I've spoken about the crisis staffs. And this is accompanied also by the intervention of paramilitary forces, i.e., groups organised in a military way and applying military techniques or tactics that do not respond to the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that were, in fact, not foreseen in the legal framework or in the concept of All People's Defence. And just to finalise, when I talk about legal framework, in the 1982 Law on All People's Defence and its amendments.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Just an observation: I get the impression that we're not making really progress, because these things were all discussed yesterday, and not once, but several times, the witness had given a similar or the same answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, but I let it go because there was unclear points as to the meaning of taking over. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, is it correct that Mr. Jesuric was chief of the Public Security Station from the elections in 1990 or sometime in 1991, when government was being established, and then further on deep into the war, as it were?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot answer the question because I'm not familiar with Mr. Jesuric's career. I know that he signed the document I quote in footnote 382.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it was the Serb Democratic Party that was in power in Bijeljina and that the police is part of the authorities, and that nothing changed there; that the only change was to declare a war presidency once the war broke out which is, indeed, an organ which is not called exactly that in the Law on National Defence, but it is an organ that is called the Presidency, and that nothing changed until the war escalated? Do you accept that there was unrest there, and there were attempts made by Muslim extremists to create chaos there, and that did not succeed, chaos did not succeed? So that's the only change?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered the question. I have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm looking for the page now. Today, you said that the Serb TO took over power in Brcko. And the Serb TO, as a newly-established organisation or formation, do you know when the Serb Territorial Defence was established?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't -- I mean, this morning I mentioned Brcko as one of the examples, but I haven't specified who took over when. Now, as for the establishment of the Bosnian Serb TO, I'm just identifying the specific document, but we see that in the course of spring 1992, decisions are taken. There are also various calls made. I spoke yesterday about the call of Mr. Karadzic during the Assembly session, I think, on the 27th of March, where he calls, indeed, the delegates to establish local Serb TO units. I mean, he doesn't call them "local Serb," but the message is clear, to establish TO units, and to subordinate those to the JNA. And if I'm not wrong, that was -- yes, indeed, I mentioned footnote 109. In my document, I also refer to the creation or the introduction of a Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Law on Defence, and this is, for example -- I mean, this starts at footnote 121.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wasn't the Serbian Territorial Defence established on the 15th or 16th of April by General Subotic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, on the -- I'm sorry. On the 15th of April, the SRBiH Presidency, and this is footnote 135 in Part 2 of the report, declares an imminent state of war as well as the full mobilisation of the SRBiH, so the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina TO. But we see from the documents I have used that units that are identified as Bosnian Serb TO or TO, but, in fact, it refers to Bosnian Serb TO, and I conclude that from the context, that such units participate in the operations aimed at taking over power or establishing Bosnian Serb control in a number of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'll tell you this: Do you know that Mr. Izetbegovic declared a general mobilisation of the Territorial Defence and the reserve forces of the police force on the 4th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible. I have not analysed that for my report. But it's important, I think, in this whole discussion to make a distinction between the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was one of the TOs foreseen in the concept of All People's Defence, i.e., the TOs were organised by republic and then on a regional and municipal level. I mean, to make a distinction between that TO and then, for example, the SRBiH TO, which is a structure that was not foreseen under the doctrine of All People's Defence. The TOs were multi-ethnic, I mean, they reflected the ethnic composition of the various republics, whereas here we see a structure that is predominantly Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, to understand military events in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the key moment is the declaration of a general mobilisation by the Croatian and the Muslim Presidency, against the will of Professor Koljevic and Ms. Plavsic. You are not taking this into account. Secondly, who broke up the Territorial Defence? Is it correct that Izetbegovic dismissed the Serb General Vukosavljevic from the post of commander of the Territorial Defence on the 8th of April?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not analysed the break-up of the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I would just like to reiterate my reference to footnote 109, which concerns a call by Mr. Karadzic during the 14th session of the Assembly of the Serbian People which occurs on the 27th of March, i.e., prior to the 8th of April, where he calls the delegates to organise the people to defend themselves and also to organise Territorial Defence and subordinate JNA to the TO. The analysis of the combat readiness, without providing dates, also highlights the role of the SDS in establishing what they call self-organising municipal and other regional units which in my understanding --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We've seen that, Mr. Theunens. Please stick to my questions. Do you know that Alija Izetbegovic, that is, the Muslim-Croatian part of the rump presidency, dismissed General Vukosavljevic from the post of the commander of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 8th of April, thus disrupting the ethnic make-up, and appointing in his place a Muslim, Hasanefendic? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm overall familiar with the events in spring 1992 in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I haven't specifically analysed, however, the changes or the decisions Mr. Karadzic is addressing now. Now, from the report -- from the documents I analysed in my report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you answered the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you know that Branko Grujic, on the 5th of April, at the level of Zvornik municipality, declared a general mobilisation, and that you noted this in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is footnote - excuse me - 428. And just to complete the answer, Branko Grujic is already commander of the SDS-led Crisis Staff of the Serb municipality from end of 1991. And these footnotes are all in Part 2 of the report, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What I want to know is: Is it correct that he declared the general mobilisation in Zvornik municipality on the 5th of April, and that this was a day after Izetbegovic's mobilisation; yes or no? And then we can agree whether the 5th comes before or after the 4th.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He calls for the mobilisation of all units of the TO of the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik on the 5th of April. And the 5th is after the 4th --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that Izetbegovic's government, on the 8th of April, not only dismissed General Vukosavljevic, and that this was a post that belonged to the Serbs in the joint authorities, and appointed Hasanefendic, and that they also declared an imminent threat of war?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is possible. But it's outside the scope of my report, so I haven't specifically analysed this for the purpose of my report. And I don't see a causal link between the events on the 4th, as Mr. Karadzic identifies them, and the events in Zvornik on the 5th and also the following days, and even before the 5th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the Serb side did the same a week later on the 15th and 16th of April, established a Serb Territorial Defence and declared an imminent threat of war?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I answered the question. I stated that, indeed, on the 15th of April they declared this imminent threat of war, and also they create a staff for the Territorial Defence or -- excuse me, the mobilisation of the Bosnian Serb Territorial Defence. But from the documents I reviewed, we see that the units identified themselves -- excuse me, or identified as Bosnian Serb TO are already established prior to the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the documents signed by General Subotic or the Presidency - I don't know - does it not say "Territorial Defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is hereby established"? How could it have existed before it was established? Can we see that? You referred to that document. I believe it's been admitted into evidence, so can we see the document referring to the establishment of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and its Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I don't doubt the document and the quotation made by Mr. Karadzic, in the sense that paragraph 1, and this follows on footnote 139 in Part 2 of the report, paragraph 1 states: "The Territorial Defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina shall be established as an armed force of the ...," and then it says "SBiH." Now, as I tried to explain from the documents I have reviewed when analysing the Bosnian Serbs taking control or taking over municipalities in Northern Bosnia, we see that there are already, prior to the 15th of April -- actually, prior to the 15th of April, mention is made of units of a TO. Sometimes it's identified as Bosnian Serb TO or "Bosnian Serb" is left out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Theunens, knowing the Law on All People's Defence, are you aware that each municipality has its own sovereign defence, it's own staff and its own TO unit, it's own Council for National Defence, and its own commander who is, ex officio, the president of the municipality, and that these units of the Territorial Defence were joint ones, and not only until the 8th, but until the 15th, when the Serbs declared their own Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the first part of Mr. Karadzic's proposition, but the key issue, and I have explained that earlier, is that we're not talking anymore about the municipalities or municipal authorities that respond to the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but we're talking about Serb or Serbian municipalities, and these are newly-established bodies that will take over -- that took over power in a number of municipalities as a result of the take-overs, replacing, then, the legally-elected municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this happened in Bijeljina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bijeljina is one of the examples, and it may well be that the same -- I mean, on the Serbian side, the same individuals remained part of the authorities, but the authorities are identified as Serbian authorities. And there is also -- I mean, there are -- non-Serbs are not anymore part of those authorities, at least not to the same extent as they were prior to these take-overs. And these authorities, obviously, do not -- these Serbian authorities do not respond to the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but to the authorities of the self-established Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know how and where, in what sort of municipality, the new Serb municipalities were established? Did that mean that the Serbs were taking over the entire municipality in question? Let's take Brcko as an example. The Serbs promulgated the Serbian Municipality of Brcko. Does that mean that they took over the entire Municipality of Brcko, derogating the authority belonging to the Serb and Muslim populations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the specific situation in Brcko, in relation to the question of Mr. Karadzic, can be found in footnote 564, Part 2 of the report, where according to the Bijeljina SJB, a report dated 19th of May, 1992, a report that is sent to the Ministry of the Interior of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I quote: "Serbian TO of Semberija and Majevica," which is an example of a Bosnian Serb TO unit, "has liberated and holds three-quarters of the Brcko town territory." I can continue: "Combat operations are being carried out in the city neighbourhood called Klanac, where enemy forces, the so-called TO of the former BiH, are mostly concentrated." So this is -- I mean, I call this "take-over," but the document, itself, uses the terminology "liberated."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does the document say that, officially, or is that something you have added?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I just read out the quotation I have included in my report, footnote 564, and that is, again, Part 2 of the report, English pages 181 to 182.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have a 65 ter number for that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is 08200.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to see that, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It doesn't say "official," Mr. Theunens. That's a word you added. It says "The Territorial Defence of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina," not "the official Bosnia-Herzegovina." I see that in the English language, and it can probably be seen in the Serbian language as well. "Enemy forces" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't remember the witness has said "official."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe it's a translation issue, but I didn't use the term "official." I used "former."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Formal" and "official," there's no difference, is there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: "Former."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, "former." Maybe they heard "formal" and translated it as "official." Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify one thing, Mr. Theunens. Do you know that before the war broke out, negotiations were going on with regard to forming large municipalities into two or three ethnically-affiliated municipalities, just as in Brussels there are smaller municipalities which were either Flemish or Walloon?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this aspect is -- falls outside the scope of my report. I haven't made a comparison between the situation in Brcko and in Brussels. I do know that the situation in Brussels is quite complicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is my thesis, Mr. Theunens: There was an ongoing political process of transformation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That process arose because we gave up the idea of remaining in Yugoslavia and accepted the idea of Bosnia-Herzegovina becoming independent on condition it was decentralised. Are you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this may well have been the case. But, again, the documents, referring now to Brcko, the documents I have included there in order to analyse the events that occurred there and the take-over, do not refer to such a political process or such negotiations. They focus on combat -- on military operations in order to establish Bosnian Serb control over large parts or even complete municipalities, large parts of municipalities or complete municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now that we're talking about Brcko, you talk about this in your report on page 104, subparagraph (h). You say, as in other towns in North-Western Bosnia in which the Bosnian Serbs took over power in April and May 1992, the take-over of Brcko was crucial for the implementation of the first strategic goal, separating the Serbian people from the two other ethnic communities, and the second strategic goal, establishing a corridor. You go on to say that the Brcko Crisis Staff, in early April 1992, based on a decision by the SDS, was established by the Serbs. Do you know that three municipalities were established in Brcko, a Serbian municipality linked to the Serbian Varos area in town, the Muslim one, the Croatian -- and the Croatian Municipality of Brcko which was called Brcko Rahic, so there was Brcko Ravne, Brcko Rahic, and the Brcko with Serbian Varos as its centre?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not on page 104. It's, in fact, on page 115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is also part of the summary. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and the summary just highlights the conclusions. But the detailed discussion on Brcko --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Comes on page 179.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours, yes. Again, what Mr. Karadzic says may well be possible. What I can conclude from the documents I looked at is -- I mean, an additional document is the footnote 562, which is a document compiled by the War Presidency, i.e., another Bosnian Serb political structure, the War Presidency of the Brcko municipality, which states that members of the Serbian forces, on the 2nd of May, 1992, have broken through all Green Beret barricades - and by "Green Beret" refers to forces controlled by the Muslims or Bosniaks - and took all important objects in the centre of the city. Now, in the context of my report, this is a vital element, and, again, I haven't seen any documents referring to the negotiations and the creation of these separate municipalities after this take-over or the Bosnian Serbs controlling the largest part of Brcko municipality and further municipalities -- the entire municipality. It may well have been that such negotiations took place before these take-over operations, but they have not affected the actual take-over or the actual -- the fact that the Bosnian Serbs take control over these municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it's not a fact, Mr. Theunens. You said yourself that the Green Berets put up barricades, they blocked the Serbs in Brcko, in Varos. Do you know that there is a part of Brcko which has always been called the Serbian Varos?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it may well be possible, but, again, it doesn't change the fact or the conclusions I base on the documents that I have reviewed; that is, that Serb forces, and their nature and composition is specified in the report, take over control over the municipality or, in the case of Brcko, according to footnote 564, three-quarters of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you now, Mr. Theunens. As in Bijeljina, the conflict was started by the Muslim side. The Green Berets blocked up the Serbian Varos part of town, and the Serbs from the regular local government prevented this. They co-operated with their Muslim colleagues in a joint government. But as they also attacked the JNA, the Green Berets lost. And from that point onwards, the Serbs controlled the Serbian part of Brcko municipality, the Croats controlled the Croatian part of Brcko municipality, and the Muslims controlled the Muslim part. There's a large Muslim village called Brezovo Polje, and nothing happened to it. That was in the Serbian part. Whereas in the Muslim part, there was a Serbian village called Bukvik which was completely destroyed, razed to the ground and the population killed. Did you know that, Mr. Theunens, that the Serbs controlled only the Serbian part of Brcko municipality, that they did no harm to the Muslims living in this larger Muslim village called Brezovo Polje which was in the Serbian part?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, footnote 564 states that -- and which is a document by the Bijeljina SJB, that Serbian TO controls three-quarters of Brcko town territory. In relation now to crimes, in footnote 577 I quote from a document by the Brcko Municipality War Presidency, that various instances of crimes are being discussed in details, and there's also later documents referring to the presence of paramilitary formations, "self-styled Chetnik units" and so on who are participating. We see also reference to Arkan. That's, for example, footnote 580, involved in, "murders for no justified reason." As to what happened or what was allegedly done by the Muslim or Bosniak forces, that was outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that in any way affect the Serbian conduct or does it help to shed some light on it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at least from a military point of view, a crime that has been committed or allegedly committed by the opposing side should not be seized as an excuse or as a pretext to allow your own forces to commit crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not talking about crimes, Mr. Theunens. You have quoted official reports of the Serbs from Brcko who are against a crime and take measures accordingly. I'm not talking about crimes. I'm speaking about defence and establishing control over their own parts of the municipality, their own neighbourhoods. Is that legitimate, if the Muslim side is committing crimes, that the Serbs should protect their own part of town?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, there are several components in this question as to these reports on crimes by Bosnian Serb police as well as the War Presidency. It is not always clear from these documents whether measures are taken against the perpetrators. Some of them, when they refer to Arkan, and, I mean, there's also mention made of names of SRS-affiliated volunteers, I have not come across any information indicating that measures were taken against these people. And now for the second part of the question, the documents I reviewed do not indicate that this take-over of control or establishing Bosnian Serb control over municipalities is a purely defensive move. When we look at the patterns of which municipalities are taken over, when, and by which forces, my conclusion is that these take-overs are part of the implementation of the six -- or at least some of the six strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Theunens, can you give us an example of what you call the take-over of municipalities that came about without a preceding attack of Muslim irregular forces; barricades, blockades, taking control of high-rise buildings, sniping, shooting? Tell us one municipality in which the Serbs took over power over their own -- in their own parts of town without that being preceded by attacks of Muslim irregular forces. Let's take Bijeljina. Was it the Muslim side who threw the first hand-grenade, set up roadblocks, positioned snipers on the tops of the highest buildings, or not, and did -- or did not the same happen in Brcko? The first -- first, there were roadblocks. Then the Serbs were sealed off. And then when the Serbs reacted, then that's called "take-over"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Karadzic does not give an accurate summary of the documents or an accurate analysis of the documents I have included in my report. According to these documents, and again they originate from JNA, Bosnian Serb police, War Presidency or Crisis Staff, occasionally reference is made to barricades that have been put up by Muslim extremists, but there is no pattern -- or there is no indication that the pattern Mr. Karadzic tries to or is depicting here also occurred in practice. I mean, these documents do not -- for the different municipalities do not systematically indicate that the take-over was a defensive act. On the contrary. The take-over goes beyond just protecting the parts that Mr. Karadzic describes as Serb parts of those municipalities. If you allow me just to complete. For example, Bosanski Samac, footnote 504, JNA 2nd Military District reports about capturing all vital facilities in Bosanski Samac, and there it is described as a preemptive move. And the take-over -- or the capture, excuse me, of vital facilities is carried out by Tactical Group 17 and units of Serb Territorial Defence and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I cannot go into Samac because it has been taken out of my indictment. But in Samac, the 8 per cent of Muslims established their own separate Territorial Defence. They had a unit of Green Berets and Patriotic League and attacked the JNA. The RS has nothing to do with Samac. They attacked the JNA, and the JNA defeated them and took them prisoner. 8 per cent of Muslims wanted to take control of Samac. But my question is: I don't care if you found the document or not. In the documents that you did find, does it unambiguously say that the first step was the setup of Muslim roadblocks in Brcko and in Bijeljina, and the second step was the clearing of these roadblocks and the setting up of control by the legal existing authorities over the municipality or parts of it? Just answer yes or no, and the Trial Chamber will find the document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents on Brcko and Bijeljina, indeed, mention roadblocks put up by what is called Green Berets or Muslim extremists. However, they do not indicate that subsequently there is a setting up of control by the legal existing authorities. No. What these documents indicate or show is that self-established Bosnian Serb structures or authorities take over power.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Show us some evidence for that. Who was the authority in Bijeljina on the day before and on the day after? The same for Bijeljina, which new structure replaced the old structure? Sir, in Brcko, the authorities dissolved because the Green Berets introduced terror, and the municipal authorities withdrew to their respective parts of the municipality, and it had been envisaged, anyway, that three municipalities should be set up. In Bijeljina, everything remained the same. Joint authorities, joint patrols, and there was no take-over of power. But let's proceed. Give us the name of any municipality where the Serb side did anything before being attacked by the Muslims? Was it in Visegrad, although it was taken out of the indictment? Was it the Serb side who started it or did the Muslim side terrorise the Serbs all year and, at the critical time, killed -- killed people, raped, and introduced terror in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has already answered the question, that the same question was posed some minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it his -- he was making a statement in relation to Bijeljina as a habit, but we have a new question about Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, Visegrad is not discussed in my report, so I cannot answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mention another municipality where the Serbs did anything before being threatened and attacked by Muslim paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as you see from my report, the purpose was not to determine who started a conflict where.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-hah. And was the purpose of your report to deny the Serbs the right to defend themselves, because you call the Serb actions as a take-over of power, a change of the situation, forceful and illegal?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have explained my understanding of the concept of take-over or what I understand under it, and I have not used the expressions "forceful" or "illegal," unless it was included in one of the documents I have used as the basis for my analysis and subsequent conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So your report pertains only to the analysis of available documents, and that does not necessarily give a complete picture of the events on the ground; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents I have included show -- I mean, show the patterns I have discussed before, and my -- I mean, the purpose of the analysis I have explained already earlier, i.e., in the scope of the report, is to see whether there were any relations between these take-overs and the authorities in the Bosnian Serb entity, or the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time, as well as to see also, and what I referred earlier, as to how and when the six strategic goals were implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that your entire report deals with strategic goals, and its purpose is not to establish the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the report goes beyond just the strategic goals, even if they are very important. It also addresses other aspects, as has been explained in the scope of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you the following: Who took over power in Bosanski Brod and how?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosanski Brod falls outside the scope of the report. But I understand, from my work outside the OTP, that Bosnian Croats and/or Muslims took over control of Bosanski Brod in spring 1992. However, in September 1992, Bosanski Brod fell to -- September/October 1992, Bosanski Brod fell to the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in Bosanski Brod, the same patterns that were -- that they tried to implement in Brcko and Bijeljina, but failed, succeeded in Bosanski Brod, and they took over power and they drove out the Serbs? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I answered that the Bosanski Brod -- events in spring 1992 in Bosanski Brod fall outside the scope of my report, so I cannot answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mention Modrica anywhere? Is it correct that in Modrica, the pattern from Bijeljina and Brcko turned out detrimentally for the Serbs? Weren't the Serbs driven out of town and a control over town established by the Green Berets and the Patriotic League? I'm referring to the Modrica municipality in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I have some references to Modrica in my report. I'm trying to locate them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who took control of Modrica first, and who drove out whom?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents I have reviewed only discuss - I mean, this is footnote 539, a report by the Command of the 17 Corps of the JNA - referred to the events after Bosnian Serbs -- or the Bosnian Serb side takes control over Modrica - and he talks -- I mean, Jankovic actually talks about the arrival of volunteers originating from Serbia in the area of Vranjak, Koprivna, covered by the Modrica municipality in March or April 1992. This is English pages 174, 175.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But who was able to take Modrica first and drive out the other side, the Serbs or the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents I have included in my report do not provide information on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But what does the next paragraph say, mentioning the 100 women and children brutally killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, but this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I didn't see the report, but does it say that that group killed them or they were killed before they arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding is that the report by Jankovic links the arrival of these -- links the killings to the arrival or the presence of these volunteers -- 40 volunteers originating from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who are the victims, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, according to the document by General -- Major-General Jankovic, and I'm quoting from the previous paragraph, people of non-Serbian nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was Jankovic at that moment; in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the whereabouts of General Jankovic at that time, but he -- I mean, it is correct that he's commander of the 17 Corps of the JNA. And at that time, the 17 Corps is being withdrawn from -- at least officially being withdrawn from Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who took control of Odzak and drove out the other side? Odzak is the adjacent municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see a reference to Odzak in the documents I quote, so I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now we're going from west to east. Is there a place called Bosanska Dubica on the Sava River? Who took over power there, and was there a take-over of power?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember that I -- I don't think I discussed events in Bosanska Dubica in my report, so I'm not able to answer the question. I may have a recollection from my work outside the OTP, but that is probably not sufficiently precise in order to provide a valuable answer to the question of Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anything happen in the Srbac municipality, which is also on the Sava, and where there are some Muslim villages? Did anything happen there, where the Serbs are the overwhelming majority and, indeed, the municipality is -- was named "Srbac" after Serbs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same answer, Your Honours. I haven't discussed -- I haven't looked into events in the municipality of Srbac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a take-over of power in Bosanska Gradiska? It's also on the Sava.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same answer, Your Honours, I mean. And I think mention was made that we move from west to east, but I have the impression that we move from east to west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no. First there's Gradiska and then there's Srbac eastward. Srbac is in the east. And a bit to the south of Srbac, in Prnjavor, was there a take-over of power?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't discussed events in Prnjavor in detail or as a specific municipality that was taken over, so I cannot answer the question. Again, some of these names obviously sound familiar, but -- because I worked on issues in Bosnia-Herzegovina throughout the conflict when I was not a member of the Office of the Prosecutor. But they are not part of the scope of my report, so I don't have a clear recollection on events in those municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you are trying to prove that there was a pattern in the activities of the Serbs. A pattern is something that should prevail in most municipalities, and here is evidence that it wasn't that way in most municipalities. The events that are attributed to the Serbs as a pattern happened in a few municipalities, where the Muslim side aspired to taking over power and driving out the Serbs, and they are Bijeljina, Brcko, unsuccessfully, and the Serb part of town, Odzak, successfully, they drove out Serbs; Modrica, successful, they drove out the Serbs, who later returned; Brod, they were successful, drove out the Serbs; Doboj, the municipality was split in two. Do you know any other municipality in the north of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, the accused now giving evidence, basically making all sorts of claims, where the witness has mentioned that he did not -- it was not part of his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're forgetting the valuable advice given by His Honour Judge Baird. How can he answer all these questions? I agree with Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. Just reformulate -- or move on or reformulate your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here's my question: You are saying that there's a pattern in the activities of the Serbs, and I put it to you that you haven't established that. Maybe you didn't have enough documents, and maybe you misunderstood the documents. And I'm putting the Defence case to you that there's no pattern in the activities of the Serbs. There were Muslim attempts to take over some municipalities and Serb responses to that. What do you say to that? Can you prove the opposite?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I concluded from the municipalities I considered, and I would say it's not just a question of numbers, but mainly, as I try to explain in this report, a question of location and size and nature of the municipality, establishing the link with the strategic goals, that in those municipalities I considered in the report, certain patterns can be identified as to how the take-overs took place, who participated in it, and what kind of events, including crimes that took place during or after the take-over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But why only in a few municipalities, why not the majority, but rather the minority? And how can you show a pattern if it isn't present in the majority? How does the exemption become a rule? It does not confirm the rule; it becomes the rule, an axiom.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've answered the questions. In those municipalities I considered, and they are listed in the report, I identified certain patterns, and I have explained which patterns these are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And your answer to the first part of his question, i.e., his defence case, is in the negative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would only be able to express myself on the municipalities Mr. Karadzic has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, as far as the municipalities you dealt with are concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Whether there were first Muslim attacks to take over some municipalities and Serbs responded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, you see the documents in my report for Bijeljina and Brcko. The documents, indeed, mention the existence of barricades by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So my question is whether the answer is no or you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't answer the question, because I haven't analysed in detail what the opposing side -- the other side did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Five minutes more, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you speak about my speeches, for example, you mention my speech in March, given on the 24th of March or the 27th of March, when the sessions of the Assembly of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina were held, do you know the context in which I speak about organising on the ground and doing whatever is necessary and so on? Why I am saying that, what is that based on? In other words - let me help you - do you know that from the 13th of February on, at least unofficially or -- or officially, but unofficially even before that, it was decided that Bosnia would have three constituent republics based on the three ethnic communities? And there is a chapter titled "The Main Political Events." Did you know of that important political event?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not come across a document discussing what appears to be a decision, but it's not clear from the question whether it's an official or unofficial decision in relation to splitting Bosnia-Herzegovina into three constituent republics with three ethnic communities. I mean, if Mr. Karadzic has a document I can review during the break, and then maybe afterwards I can be of assistance in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that I made statements, and we have that in the newspapers, not division, but transformation, and we did get that transformation by way of an offer from the European Community, and the 18th of March we accepted the constitutional principles of this future Bosnia-Herzegovina? That was the most important political event in Bosnia-Herzegovina that we all celebrated as the salvation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 18th of March. Lord Carrington and Ambassador Cutileiro, after several months of work, we achieved this, definitely, some things that would not be changed. The only thing that remained was to define borders, then the question of the army and the referendum, so three issues. Are you aware of this main event and that every speech of mine should be viewed in that context, in that light, from the 14th of February until the 1st of April?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, from my work outside the OTP, I'm familiar with the efforts of Lord Carrington as well as Ambassador Cutileiro and the Cutileiro Plan, which spoke about the division of Bosnia-Herzegovina in kind of a Swiss structure. But, again, from the material that I reviewed for my report, the importance Mr. Karadzic is now attributing to these -- to this plan and these efforts, this importance is not reflected in the documents I reviewed. No. Instead, we see that -- and I analysed what was happening on the Bosnian Serb side, that efforts are made already prior and during the time-period mentioned by Mr. Karadzic to establish military structures, to create an own Bosnian Serb TO, to arm them, to co-operate with the JNA, in order to implement certain goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Theunens, that is total confusion. I cannot deal with your limitations. You just talk about the documents that were accessible to you, and you're talking about the totality of the picture. Who selected these documents for you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we have heard the answer. We'll have a -- it's time to have a break. We'll break for 25 minutes and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Excuse me, Mr. President. I don't mean to disturb you with something small, but we've run into a problem this morning because security has interpreted a previous decision that you've made so that our case manager would not be allowed to have contact with Dr. Karadzic in the holding cell while the expert is also here, and I'm referring to a decision on the 20th of August, 2010, in which you did state that at any time, only two people, in addition to Dr. Karadzic, would be permitted in the holding cell when the expert was here. And then you went on to say that further questions or clarification could be addressed to the Registry through the "proces" officer. And since that decision, on every day that we've had an expert here, we've also managed to have the case manager in the room, holding cell, assisting us, but today the security guards, relying on your decision of the 20th of August, 2010, prohibited that. And it's difficult for Dr. Karadzic to manage to prepare the next session when we don't have the person who's in charge of the documents with us, so we would ask that either you modify your order so that one additional person can be in the holding cell or else you order that Dr. Karadzic not be taken to the holding cell during the breaks and we work in the courtroom, where all of us can be present. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll look into the matter during the course of this session and get back to you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us move away from this topic, and perhaps we'll go back to it later, the question of patterns. On page 157, I think -- we merged a few documents here, so there is a problem with the page numbers and the footnotes. "The Participation of Volunteers from BiH and the Conflict in Croatia," that's the chapter, and it's sub-chapter (e), and it says: "On the 22nd of September, 1991, or before that date, the president of the Serb Democratic Party, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, issued an order to all secretariats for national defence in the Serb autonomous municipalities." Do you remember that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the document, Your Honours, but it would help me if I had the footnote number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we'll see the number of the footnote was 503, unless that has also been changed, disrupted.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I have found the document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you accepted this document and you took a certain position on the basis of the document, and you made it part of your report, as a significant document; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I included -- I did select the document for my report without drawing specific conclusions on the report, as just to refer to its contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But where are we, in terms of the report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is in Part 1, Your Honours, footnote 502, 503, these two footnotes. Part 1, it's English page -- at least the version I have, 159, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think I was looking at Part 2.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 00957 in e-court, please, ERN number 795. That's the most legible. I have three variants here. 795 is the most legible one. If you have 95, that could be even better, the Serbian version. It's all right, I have it on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So do you claim that this is an authentic document? Did you take it as an authentic document? Did you take it to be an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was my understanding that this document has also been used in other trials, and even admitted there, and that is why I decided to include it in my report. I have not been able to establish the -- I mean, to physically establish the authenticity of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to present some elements to you. There is no registration number. The adjective "Serb," "Serb people," is not written in capital letters in the language, and that kind of thing could not have happened to me. Now, let's look at the rest. It is being sent to the Secretariat of National Defence, SNO, Secretariat for National Defence, SAO Krajina, Romanija, and North-Eastern Bosnia. Mr. Theunens, in the SAOs, are there secretariats for national defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for this document, I haven't seen any specific references to secretariats for national defence, bearing in mind, however, that what we see in the newly-established structures, that sometimes what I would call old names, i.e., names of structures that existed in the SFRY and, in this particular case where defence is concerned, under the doctrine of All People's Defence, that sometimes these names are used even if we are talking about different structures. And this morning I believe we reviewed some documents where the use -- where these secretariats for defence, national defence, or people's defence at municipal level or regional level, could be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is preeminently military subject matter. Do you agree that the Secretariat for National Defence is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I didn't understand your question, Mr. Karadzic. Did this order -- or this document says it was sent to SNO Krajina, Romanija, North-Eastern Bosnia, et cetera, where can we find it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the text, I'm reading the Serbian version: "At a crucial point -- at a critical point for the Serbian people," and Serbian is capitalised, which is not right in our language, "I hereby order that you provide assistance to our liberators and units from Serbia and Montenegro by sending in our volunteers and providing them with material and moral support in their mission to create an alliance of Serbian states. "In the SNO of the autonomous districts of Krajina, Romanija and North-Eastern Bosnia," I cannot read this, "you eliminate Ustasha and Muslim elements that are preventing the establishment of a fair and just single Serb government in the pan-Serbian lands. "If these just and humane desires of the Serbian people are opposed, show no mercy (an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth). "Establish court-martials for these purposes." This is a forgery, a brazen one at that, and deceit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: First of all, do you agree that secretariats of national defence are under the Federal Secretariat of National Defence in Yugoslavia and that they keep records, military records, for conscripts, and that they are immediately responsible -- directly responsible to the Federal Secretariat of National Defence, that is, the Ministry of Defence of Yugoslavia; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it should be, and that's how it should have been or was under the -- when the SFRY still existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of September -- rather, here it says that it was received on the 22nd of September, for Bosnia, Yugoslavia did exist. Can the head of a political party issue orders to the Secretariat of National Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the legislation that was applicable in the SFRY, no. But we see that later on, when, for example, the Bosnian Serbs or the Serbs in Croatia start to establish their own structures, as I explained earlier, sometimes they still used the names as they were applicable under the SFRY, even if the composition and the activities and, most importantly, the relationship between these new structures and the superior level have changed; i.e., they're not responding anymore to republican authorities, but they're responding to Serbian authorities, for example, municipalities -- Serbian municipalities to Serbian SAOs or autonomous regions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, Dr. Karadzic put to you that that document was a forgery. Are you in a position to answer one way or the other to that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I mentioned, I'm not in a position to physically examine the document in order to see whether it's authentic or not. However, when I selected the document, I was under the understanding it has been used in other -- in related trials before and that such objections had not been raised at that occasion, or at least I'm not familiar with any objection raised in relation to this document during a prior trial here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That makes things even worse for those trials, or, rather, those accused persons, Mr. Theunens. So the head of a party at that point in time -- I mean, there is no Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in September 1991 anyway. And what about the SAOs that had just been declared and had no organs whatever; did they have secretariats for national defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I answered the question already, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You spoke about the municipalities, clear about the municipality level. But at the level of an SAO, is there a secretariat for national defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, based on the documents I reviewed, I do not believe that -- and, again, I haven't analysed the SAOs in detail and I haven't looked at the ARK, for example, but I don't have an impression that such bodies existed, even if there may be an example that -- examples that the name was used for bodies that had a similar role at the SAO level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did that exist in September? Did that exist ever at the level of SAOs, a secretariat for national defence ?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have not answered the question. I am asking you where. If you don't know, say you don't know, and then let's move on. On the 21st of September, was there an SAO Krajina then?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer the question because I haven't looked at the -- I mean, an AR Krajina, or, excuse me, an Autonomous Region Krajina, I don't know when it was established, but in Bosnia-Herzegovina there was never an SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there an SAO North-Eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is the question whether it existed or whether it existed on the 21st of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of September and ever.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have included in my report a decision from the 21st of November, 1991. That is footnote 77, which consists of the verification of the decision for the proclamation of Serb autonomous districts, SAOs, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there mention is made of an SAO Northern Bosnia. Now, the document does not allow to determine whether any of these SAOs, or autonomous regions as far as Krajina is concerned, when they were actually established. And it's footnote 77 in Part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that North-Eastern Bosnia takes the territory -- or actually is comprised of the territory of Semberija and Majevica, and was it called the SAO of Semberija and Majevica?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever heard of "all Serbian lands," as is written here, "sve srpske zemlje"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The expression "Serbian lands" is regularly used or was regularly used at the time. I don't remember seeing "all Serbian lands" as a specific expression.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever come across any information to the effect that we had court-martials?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the establishment of a -- I mean, a system of military discipline, of military justice, within the VRS. Now, I was not able to establish, when preparing this report, whether such a system also existed for the Bosnian Serb TO or whether the existing structures of the SFRY armed forces, i.e., the JNA, were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did court-martials ever exist? Were they ever established, even during the course of the war? And how can I then ask you whether there were court-martials in peacetime in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, during the preparation of my report, I haven't come across documents, to my recollection now, that discuss the issue of court-martials, except for this one document we're looking at now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you accept that, that these are sufficient elements to say that this is not an authentic document, that it is a forgery rather?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I agree with Mr. Karadzic that there are a number of factors that cast potential doubt about the contents of the document.
