Now, again, as I mentioned earlier, and I think I mentioned it twice, that those who drafted documents not always -- were not always consistent in using the correct terminology. This document is, indeed, signed by Dr. Karadzic, but it may well have been drafted by somebody else and he signed it. So taking that into account, yeah, one would be cautious in using the document, but I cannot conclude that it's a forgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we have a registration number of the register, that is, so that it can be checked whether it was created in the SDS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the document now, but I don't think it included a registration number. Now, I have seen more documents without a number from various structures and different levels, so it is, again, a factor to take into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Up-load the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 957.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is no number in the register, where the address and the letterhead of the party is; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Another question in relation to this document: In how many municipalities or secretariats of national defence was this document found as a document that had arrived?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot answer the question. To my understanding, the OTP has only one version of it, but we would have to verify the databases, also establish how it was obtained, and then check whether additional versions of this document would be available. When I say "additional versions," additional copies, actually, i.e., received by other addressees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, according to what we were just able to find out, this version was seized from Bihac in 1996 by a member of this office. But there seems to be also another version here seized also from the AID Bihac in 1999, and we can look into this, whether -- how -- whether we have yet other versions. We can check that, but from the courtroom it's rather difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. If the interpreters could be kind enough to read out the first line on the left top. Does it say -- is it: "Received from"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: "Received from."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, it seems this has been added to the document, because everything else is in Cyrillic, but this text is in Latin script.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And typed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Theunens, that the Serb Democratic Party won power in 47 municipalities and that Bihac was not among the municipalities where the Serb Democratic Party had won the election?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, Mr. Karadzic mentioned that yesterday. I'm not fully familiar with that. I do remember that in Bihac there was no significant Serbian presence. But the fact that it was received by AID Bihac doesn't have to mean that AID, which was the Bosniak or Muslim Intelligence Service, seized or found the document in Bihac. We would have to see how the AID obtained the document, and from where, and whom, and how.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This 957, together with the allegation that it is a result of a forgery?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, and it's part of the report and a footnote in Mr. Theunens' report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it there's no opposition from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1586, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the summary, paragraph 24, you say, and I'll read it out in Serbian: "In the period from January to March 1992, the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina was characterised by a high degree of confusion both as regards the future status of BH within the SFRY as well as the role of the JNA in BH ..." And so on and so forth. You say: "By March in 1992, at the latest, Serb-dominated JNA units were openly carrying out operations, protecting, arming, and helping in other ways the Bosnian Serbs and on the areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina claimed by the Serbs."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note they were unable to find the precise reference in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it says: "At the same time, the commands of the 2nd Military District commands of the JNA --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would could Mr. Karadzic slow down when reading, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You need to slow down. His reading out is para 24 of the executive summary. I'm not sure the interpreters were provided with the report. Slow down, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the report be brought up in e-court, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we have the reports with us. You can put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first question is: This high degree of confusion you established from January to March 1992, did it arise suddenly in January 1992 or was it the result of the development of a crisis?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it did not arise suddenly. It is a result of several factors; obviously, the independence of Slovenia, followed by the conflict -- the armed conflict in Croatia, as well as then activities by various ethnic groups in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as actions of the SFRY Presidency and other leadership bodies all contribute to creating a situation whereby, basically, the future status of Bosnia-Herzegovina is unclear and there exists confusion about this future status.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware of the constant statements by Stjepan Mesic, who was later the Croatian president, but at that time I think he was the speaker of the Croatian Parliament, his statements to the effect that the war front would spill over from Croatia into Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not specifically familiar with the statements of Stjepan Mesic. But many senior politicians on all sides made statements as to the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and from these statements, it was clear that everybody wanted something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the war in Croatia and Slovenia waged by a newly-established republican army composed of the police force, as their core, the National Guard Corps, and the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not analysed the conflict in Slovenia. I have discussed the conflict in Croatia, or aspects of the conflict in Croatia, in Part 1 of the report, where I analysed the -- again, the establishment of Bosnian -- of Serbian armed structures in Croatia and their relations with the JNA. I know from my work for another trial, the trial of Gotovina, Cermak and Markac, about, indeed, the creation of the ZNG and the transformation of the TO, or the split of the TO of the Republic of Croatia into actual, actually, ZNG, local Serb TO, and related structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the summary, paragraph 1, towards the end of the paragraph you say: "The task of the armed forces of the SFRY was to protect the independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity and social order established by the Constitution of the SFRY." So you were looking at events in the context of paragraph 1 of the summary. According to what you wrote here, does it follow that the armed forces of the SFRY were duty-bound to prevent one-sided secession, that is, breaches of the independent sovereignty, territorial integrity, and social order established by the Constitution of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Karadzic, when quoting from paragraph 1, provided the de jure mission of the SFRY armed force as is, indeed, established in the -- was established in the 1974 Constitution and confirmed in the 1982 Law on All People's Defence, but I've also highlighted in my report that, again, on the basis of the documents I reviewed, in the course of 1991, the mission of what remains of the SFRY armed forces in Croatia changes. And this is, for example, illustrated by the former Federal Secretary for People's Defence, Army General Kadijevic, who identifies, in a very precise manner, the different phases in the conflict in Croatia, whereby in the last phase, starting at the latest in the summer of 1991, he states that the JNA starts to fight in support of the Serbs in Croatia, which means that this constitutional goal and mission has changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I didn't intend to deal with this aspect, but since you mention it, Mr. Theunens: Is it correct that changes in the de facto situation, as opposed to the de jure situation, resulted from the illegal attacks on the JNA, and that the JNA was able to survive only in those areas that wanted it there, and those were the Serb areas in Croatia? In other words, was the Constitution changed, and then the role of the JNA changed accordingly, or was it due to forcible actions by the illegal armies of Slovenia and Croatia that the JNA reduced its de jure role to its de facto stay in those areas which accepted it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Constitution was not changed. Now, as to the reasons for these de facto changes, Mr. Karadzic has presented his views. The documents I have reviewed provide another picture; that is, that a commonality develops in the goals of the Serbs in Croatia and of the JNA, together, of course, with also the assistance of the Government of the Republic of Serbia, assistance in organising and arming local Serb armed structures, consisting of TO and police, as well as the participation of volunteers/paramilitary groups from Serbia in the conflict in Croatia, whereby all these formations, together with the JNA, most often under single command, fight or conduct military operations to establish Serb control over areas with a significant Serb presence or areas that are considered Serb for -- by these -- by the Serbian side, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You are a scholar, Mr. Theunens, and what you are saying now is political propaganda. What I'm asking you is the following: Did someone order the JNA, according to the Constitution and the law, to desist from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When you say, made a statement, you should give the opportunity to respond. Mr. Theunens, you were referred to as making a political propaganda.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not my intention, Your Honour. I'm just summarising what I have written in my report, Part 1 on the conflict in Croatia, whereby that is, again, based on contemporaneous sources, JNA documents, documents from local Serb -- Krajina Serb TO, Krajina Serb MUP, the book by Army General Kadijevic, the book by the former acting chairman of the Federal Presidency, Jovic, as well as other documents. The documents are there, so it can easily be verified that it's not propaganda I'm making here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you want to say that the JNA was able to and allowed to derogate this constitutional decision on its own -- on its own initiative or, rather, its constitutional obligation before any changes or amendments were made to the Constitution? Was the JNA able and allowed to say, on its own initiative, I no longer want to carry out my constitutional role? You are an expert on the army. Can an army do this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the JNA, as a component of the SFRY armed forces, was at the time subordinated to the SFRY Presidency. There were a number of changes in the SFRY Presidency. We also know, from the book by Mr. Jovic, that in addition to the SFRY Presidency, there were meetings between not only members of the Presidency, but members of the Presidency together with the leadership of the Republic of Serbia and Montenegro, and they all shared the same goal, which was not the constitutional goal for the SFRY armed forces, and this goal was communicated to the military -- to the military in order to be implemented. And I spoke also about the assistance the Government of the Republic of Serbia provided in arming and organising local Serb armed structures, consisting of police and Territorial Defence, in --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you answer my question, please, can you answer my question? This is a question of doctrine. Can an army --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm losing time. We're wasting time, Your Excellency. I have no time. I didn't ask what happened in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your answer is not the one just simply answered by either yes or no. That's why if the witness needs to expand, he should be allowed to do so. It's for you to plan how to efficiently conduct your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I simplify my question? In 1991, the JNA or any other army in the world, was it able to redefine its constitutional role on its own, without any amendments being made to the Constitution, and was it able to say, I no longer want to carry out my constitutional role?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that the JNA would not have been deployed on territories inhabited by Serbs -- or, rather, inhabited by Muslims and Croats who recognised the Yugoslav institutions? Did you ever establish any such thing?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't -- I'm not sure I understand the question. I would assume you're talking now about Bosnia-Herzegovina. But which time-period are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am now referring to Croatia also. Did the JNA withdraw to Serb territories because there were Serbs there or because there was no one attacking them there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as for Croatia, there have been attacks against JNA garrisons, and that was well published -- publicised in various open sources. But I have not been able to -- I mean, the research I did does not show that there is, in all cases, a causal link between the redeployment of the JNA as well as the combat operations conducted by the JNA, on one hand, and, on the other hand, attacks against its barracks. I can give you one example just from the top of my head. The JNA enters Baranja, Eastern Croatia, in August 1991 without any military necessity, because there is no -- if there is, it's very limited JNA presence in that part of Croatia, and there are no attacks at that -- prior to this deployment of additional JNA forces in that part of Croatia. And there are other examples. I would, just to cut it short, refer to footnotes 381 and 382 of Part 1 of the report to explain the political background -- or aspects of the political background to the change in mission of the JNA in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that up to the 6th of April, 1992, Bosnia and Herzegovina was part of Yugoslavia, both de jure and de facto?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this question is outside the scope of my report. From the knowledge I had prior to joining the OTP, I would agree with Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did the JNA withdraw from Slovenia and Croatia to Bosnia, which was a part of the territory of Yugoslavia? And is it correct that when it did so, it avoided Eastern Herzegovina, which was inhabited mostly by Croats, because it foresaw that it would not be welcome there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA withdrew from Slovenia in -- after the events of July -- I mean, June/July 1991. As for Croatia, the situation is more complicated, in the sense that there is an official withdrawal of the JNA. Obviously, the JNA withdraws from those parts of Croatia where there's no significant Serb presence or those parts of Croatia that are not under Serb control. But the parts that remain under Serb control, we know that there is an agreement on the Vance Plan, and part of the implementation of the Vance Plan is to demilitarise the so-called UNPAs, the United Nations Protected Areas that have been established by the Vance Plan, but in practice, and that can be found in Part 1 of the report, JNA personnel that had been born in the area, but also originating from other parts of the former Yugoslavia, stays in the area, and they also leave equipment behind. And after, say, April 1992, they continue to provide personnel and logistic support to the Serb -- to the local Serb TO, which is subsequently transformed into the SVK. And as I also mentioned, there is support by the Republic of Serbia to the minister of interior forces of the Serb entity in Croatia, i.e., the RSK. Now, for Bosnia -- I mean, some of these units are then withdrawn to Bosnia-Herzegovina or redeployed in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but I have no detailed information as to why they would not be sent to Eastern Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I was referring to Western Herzegovina because that's the Croatian part. But let me ask you this: Is it correct that the command structure of the Croatian Army and the Croatian Territorial Defence was composed of officers who had left the JNA, and was this the case with the Muslim army also?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I know that Croat or Muslim or Bosniak officers who served in the JNA, that a number of them left the JNA for various reasons to join the armed forces that were created in their entity or among their ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I put all these questions in order to lead up to the following: What is the standpoint taken in your report towards the fact that the Serb Democratic Party, instead of developing its own party armed force, supported the JNA throughout this time and supported the response -- or, rather, supported the mobilisation call of the JNA? Was this according to the law?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, as we saw, for example, in the document -- the report General Kukanjac sends on the 20th of March on the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina, we see that a commonality develops in the goals pursued by the SDS and the JNA. And Kukanjac, for example, talks about how the Serbian people, including the SDS leadership, has embraced the JNA, even if there are also examples of criticism or attacks of SDS members against the JNA because they want to have their own forces or are suspicious of what they call the Communist JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Serb Democratic Party have its own forces, or were young Serbian men in the JNA, whereas Croat and Muslim young men were in units under the command of their own ethnic leaders?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a complicated question, Your Honours, because we see that the -- that the SDS or the leadership of the SDS, including Mr. Karadzic, calls for establishment and mobilisation of local Serb TO units, whereby they asked the municipalities -- the Serb municipalities to send the young men to these TO units. I mean, prior to that there have been calls to send the young men to the JNA, but at one moment in time there is a change, in spring 1992, whereby calls are made to send these mobilised young men to the TO and whereby the Bosnian Serb TO is to be subordinated to the JNA. So there is a -- there is an evolution. And just to finalise, for example, footnote 71 in Part 2 explains the relationship or the role of the SDS in this process as seen in the VRS analysis of combat readiness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, since you've broadened this, I'll put the following to you: Up to the 27th of March, the standpoint of the SDS was that young Serb men who supported the SDS should respond to the JNA call-up. Was this a legal and legitimate standpoint, bearing in mind that the JNA was the only legitimate armed force?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the point of view of the SDS as being presented now by Mr. Karadzic, I mean, prior to the 27th of March corresponds with the existing legislation in the SFRY; that is that, okay, if there is a call-up by the JNA for mobilisation, then those who are to be mobilised should respond and should join the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. You say that in late March, at the Assembly, I launched an appeal to set up a territorial defence. Do you know that on the 18th of March, we were given the final right to establish our constituent unit, and within that unit, we would have the authority over the TO, and possibly over an army, or if not an army, then at least a national guard? The issue of a joint army was put off for a later date. Do you know that I made that recommendation in the context of the agreements reached with the European Community?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in order to answer this question, I would have to review these agreements. And I haven't had the opportunity it this far, to do it at this stage, so I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You're critical towards the SDS because of its policy in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you think that it would be necessary for you to know more about the main political processes and events, including the Conference on Bosnia-Herzegovina, to make such conclusions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not critical towards SDS or any other party or organisation. In my report, I just try to highlight or to illustrate the activities of the SDS on the basis of the documents that I could find in the database -- databases available to the OTP. When I say "the activities of the SDS," the activities in relation to establishing military structures as well as the role played in take-over of municipalities. Yeah, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to put forward a series of facts from political life that brought about the confusion that you noticed from January 'til March, and I will not be angry if you do not know about them. It's only important for us to hear if you knew or didn't know about them. Did you know that the SDS and the SDA shared the same view with regard to the change of the political system and the preservation of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not analysed the views of the SDA on the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the preservation of Yugoslavia at that moment in time, so I cannot answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the SDA, the SDS and the HDZ won over 90 per cent of power, and the SDS had about one-third of power in all of Bosnia at the central level?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember from my work outside the OTP that during the last elections in Bosnia-Herzegovina, I mean, prior to the conflict, that the - I would call it - ethnically-based parties had won an overwhelming majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the SDA, as early as late January 1991, changed its attitude toward Yugoslavia, and in February and March tried to push a decision on the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina through the Assembly, which was a first step towards independence, and that it was prevented by a constitutional mechanism; namely, the Council on Ethnic Equality, in which decisions are taken by consensus?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not 100 per cent familiar with this change in attitude, as Mr. Karadzic describes it. It falls outside the scope of my report, so I cannot comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on to military issues. Did you know on the 31st of March, 1991, a decision was adopted to establish a secret army called the Patriotic League, and on the 30th of April, it was, indeed, set up? It was a military formation of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the existence of a formation called -- an armed formation called Patriotic League and its links with the SDA, but, again, it's outside the scope of this report so I cannot provide any additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that on 10 June, the Council for the Defence of the Muslims was set up, and that was a political -- or the political staff of the Patriotic League in Sarajevo? You are aware that the Serb Assembly had set up a council for national security, which was an advisory body, in 1992, and did you know that a party body, which was mono-ethnic, was set up by the Muslim side on 10 June 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not familiar with the decision nor the -- the decision on the 10th of June, 1991. I can just illustrate that the Council for National Security, or the National Security Council, was established by the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 27th of March, 1992, and that's footnote 89 in Part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that in late June 1991, Presidents Kucan and Tudjman, as well as the president of the collective Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Izetbegovic, reached -- or actually agreed on a secret military pact against Yugoslavia and the JNA? This is a military matter.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's, indeed, a military matter, but it's out -- it falls outside the scope of my report, and I don't have any detailed recollection of such an alleged secret military pact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in July and August 1991, the Serbian side gave up on the idea of regionalisation, the SAOs, and other political steps, in favour of an historic Serbian-Muslim agreement offered by a minor Muslim party, but it was supported by President Izetbegovic, and these activities prevailed -- or these talks lasted or went on in July and August?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's the same answer as the previous question. I mean, this is not a military matter, but it's -- it falls outside the scope of my report, and I have no specific recollection about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to your section "Important political Events." You dealt with them. You devote an entire section to that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the selection of main political events I made is based on the scope of the report, and that's why selection was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, and this is a military matter, that the SDA party, around about the 26th of September, decided to step up the clandestine monitoring of the conduct and the structure of JNA in Bosnia-Herzegovina and, of course, the SDS and the Serbs? Did you know that the SDA party began to spy on the JNA, which was its legitimate army?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, this is a matter that falls outside the scope of my report, and, therefore, I'm not in a position to provide additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know or have you heard of Sefer Halilovic? Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I know who Sefer Halilovic is. He used to be Chief of the General Staff of the ABiH, but he was removed, I think, in the course of 1993. While I was working for the OTP, I did not conduct any professional activities in relation to Sefer Halilovic or activities of the ABiH, but I know this from my professional activities prior to joining the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Sefer Halilovic, before he publicly became the commander of the BH Army, was the secret commander of the Patriotic League, and that in late September had staffs in 98 municipalities, as well as 9 regional staffs, and a total of about 100.000 soldiers? By March 1992, that had grown to 103 municipalities and 120.000 men.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this falls outside the scope of my report. I have not analysed the establishment, organisation, or activities of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did the Serbs live in a vacuum so that their conduct can be viewed without taking into account the context of their opponents? How could you analyse the Serb activities without paying attention to the fact that in 103 municipalities, out of which in 47 the SDS was in power, civil war was being prepared?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the fact that the scope of my report focuses on a particular aspect does not mean that anything else that occurred is irrelevant or so for me, but it falls outside the scope. The scope of the report is very clear, and, I mean, there's plenty of publications available where a particular aspect of a conflict or of an issue can be studied and analysed, and conclusions can be drawn without having to analyse or drawing conclusions on the activities of others who may have been involved in the situation of a conflict or a particular issue. The title of the report is also very clear; it's not the history or an analysis of the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is an analysis of a role of an individual, i.e., Mr. Karadzic, in relation to his authority over the Bosnian Serb TO and the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you also dealt with the political background of the Serbian activities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the approaching of the JNA, in spite of ideological differences, and then there were mobilisation call-ups and so on. Did you come across our frequent warnings that civil war was underway -- or, rather, was being prepared, and that we were looking for political answers to what was going on right in front of our nose? Were our acts justified and sensible or, as suggested by the report, some rebellious conduct, without cause, that disturbs the idyllic co-existence in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I talk about political aspects, it is to explain -- or first establish and explain the role the SDS, or other political bodies established by the Bosnian Serbs, played in organising, arming and supporting military structures they had established. It's not my intention -- or it was not my intention, it's not -- again, it falls outside the scope to determine whether any of these activities were justified or unjustified, or sensible or not sensible, and I haven't spoken in my report about an idyllic co-existence in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Again, that's outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Theunens, implicitly your report suggests that the Serbs engaged in illegal activities that threatened the peace. But in our speeches, acts, appeals and press releases, there is enough evidence that what the Serbs are pointing out was true, that a secret Muslim army was being set up that was going to launch a civil war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Did you ever ask yourself why the Serbs were saying what they were saying and doing what they were doing? Did anybody prohibit you from trying to find the causes for that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, nobody prohibited me nor requested me to address the causes of the events in Bosnia-Herzegovina in my report, so I haven't drawn any conclusions as to who was responsible or who started what, where, and when. What I have done is on the basis of the -- on the basis of the documents that were available to me and within the scope of the report, I have attempted to analyse the role of Mr. Karadzic as the highest political authority over the Bosnian Serb TO and the VRS, focusing on two aspects: his command authority, i.e., the ability to issue orders and verify their implementation, and, secondly, his situational awareness. That may be a very restricted scope, but that's how the situation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Nonetheless, in the chapter about the Territorial Defence of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in subsection (b), the most important political events, you say that the Bosnian Serbs, led by the SDS, established parallel political structures in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the culmination of which was the proclamation of a separate Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 9th of January, 1992. You say that on 24 October, we established the Assembly of the Serbian people. Item 1 and sub-items (a) and (b) say that the Assembly of the Serbian people expressed its full support of the JNA, and so on. Did you establish whether our constitutional rights had been infringed upon, whether we had given the Muslims and Croats a chance to correct their mistake? Did we respond by setting up our own assembly? Were all of our actions responses to the illegal moves of the other side or do you think that is not important?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I've tried to explain -- explain in previous answers, these issues fall outside the scope of my report. Now, the fact that they fall outside the scope of my report does not include any judgement as to their relevance or importance. I will also say that establishing whether or not constitutional rights had been infringed upon falls outside my professional knowledge. It would be more something to be addressed maybe by a constitutional expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Apart from the constitutional issue, you do not know the facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I may know some facts, based on my professional activities outside the OTP, i.e., prior to joining the OTP, but I have not covered them in my report. And that's why I systematically answer that I'm not able to provide any additional information, because my recollection also is quite weak of these other events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which parallel structures of the Bosnian Serbs were effectively in existence before April 1992? Which parallel structures were put into effect? Do the SAOs have power? Does the Assembly of the Bosnian Serbs effectively equal a council of the peoples, or did any parallel institution actually get off the ground before April 1992 and have real power?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, all I can say, Your Honours, is that a number of bodies are established prior to April 1992. You can find them in the section that discusses main political developments. We have the Assembly. We have the proclamation of SAOs. We also have a decision on establishment of a government. Now, coming -- answering the question whether they had power or not, the Council for National Security, for example, is established on the 27th of March, 1992, issues certain decisions, even if the reports I have on the activities of the Council for National Security only date from after the 1st of April. Now, the 1st of April is when the take-over of Bijeljina takes place. It is reasonable to assume that if the SDS and Arkan, according to the JNA, take control -- excuse me, remove barricades by -- erected by what was called Green Berets and then also take control of the municipality, that these structures and their co-operation must have been established prior to the 1st of April. I mean, from a military point of view, it is not something you decide the 1st of April, in the morning, and then you move ahead. You need to plan and organise it. In Bijeljina, there is also other groups who participate in the take-over, and these activities have to be planned and organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Theunens, that in Bijeljina, the legitimate authorities were able to defend themselves against the Green Berets, and you are still saying that somebody took over power from somebody else. Tell the Trial Chamber who took over power from who, and why don't you prove -- how can you prove that Bijeljina was taken over?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Again, asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's come up again and it's wrong again, and that's why I'm asking the witness to provide some evidence for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We do not have the luxury of time to revisit the same issue again and again. I think it's time to take a break. Mr. Robinson, I have been now advised that Security is not opposed to a third team member meeting with Mr. Karadzic in the holding cell during the breaks. Therefore, on the days when the Chamber has allowed a Defence expert to be present in the courtroom, this expert will be allowed to meet with Mr. Karadzic in the holding cell, in addition to other -- in addition to the other two team members.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, and our thanks to Security as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break for 50 minutes and resume at 25 past 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.33 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'll try to go through some matters which are important to me very quickly. Please don't feel you're under attack if there's something you don't know. You received the documents you received, but I want to know what you took into account and what not. Do you agree that the Serbian side in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and not just the SDS, but all the assemblymen in the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, gave up the idea of remaining in Yugoslavia and agreed to remain in Bosnia-Herzegovina, provided it was decentralised, and this was already in late 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just two elements, Your Honours. First of all, it's not a question about the documents I received. I selected the documents myself from the material that was available to me in the databases held by the OTP. There were no restrictions imposed on that access. As to the second part of the question, I cannot comment on that because I didn't conduct a political analysis. I conducted a military analysis. So the proposition made by Mr. Karadzic falls outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, by now you should know what the scope of this witness's report is. I consider such questions as wasting precious cross-examination time. Posing questions is -- the questions, themselves, are no value at all unless confirmed by the witness. You'll have another opportunity to put your case to another witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, if you had a little more faith in me, you would see that this is leading to my goal, and the goal is to see whether the six strategic goals were something new in Serbian politics or whether this was all agreed on with the international community and the Muslims and Croats in Bosnia as of late 1991, because I'm now moving on to the topic of the strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you know that the six strategic goals, which you said you felt were being taken into account and something was being done about them before May, do you know that except for the Strategic Goal 2, they were all part of the negotiations in the Conference on Bosnia and Herzegovina from the moment we gave up the idea of remaining in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot answer the question. It may well be the case, but I have not analysed the activities of the International Conference on the former Yugoslavia, nor the activities of Lord Carrington or Mr. Cutileiro in the framework of that conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you said that the Army of Republika Srpska was established with the aim and task of implementing the six strategic goals; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not think I have worded it like that. It is correct, however, and that is what I have showed in the report, that the six strategic goals formed the basis for the operations conducted by the VRS throughout its existence until the conclusion of a peace agreement in November 1995. And there was a cease-fire just prior to that, but -- and that is also visible through the directives that are issued by the Main Staff, as well as two directives issued by Mr. Karadzic, as supreme commander, and the orders of subordinate units, as we discussed during the examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is how things stand, Mr. Theunens: Was the first strategic goal the ethnic separation of the Serbs from the other two ethnic communities, and was it established before May 1992, before the outbreak of the war, in the course of the conference; yes or no? Did we achieve the European Community proposing that there should be three ethnic constituent units; Serb, Croatian and Muslim? If you don't know this and if you did not take this into account, how can we consider your entire report at all?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, and I'm now referring to footnote 163 in Part 2 of the report, when Mr. Karadzic presents the strategic goals at the 16th Assembly session, he states, in relation to the first goal, that -- and now first my words. I say that it is aimed at separating, and now I start the quotation. "... from those who are our enemies and who have used every opportunity, especially in this century, to attack us, and who would continue with such practices if we were to continue to stay together in the same state." This is how this goal is presented by Mr. Karadzic to the members of the Assembly of the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina. He doesn't make any reference to any alleged reference to this goal or to this separation in any peace plans presented by the European Union -- or the European Community or other international organisation at that time. Again, when reviewing the material, both the Bosnian Serb strategic goals as well as the directives for further operations, none of these make reference to any international endorsement of these goals, let alone their implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did not ethnic intolerance lead the Slovenes and Croats to leave Yugoslavia and the Muslims to leave the rump Yugoslavia, as they called it, and we said to them, publicly, If you don't want to live with us in Yugoslavia because you're afraid you'll be out-voted, we don't want to live with you in Bosnia because then you will out-vote us? In every war, the Muslims took the side of the Croats and Germans and attacked us. Sir, this was said in public, We can't stay with you in the same community because you have taken Muslim fundamentalism as the basis -- as the foundation of your state. Did you know that this was the fundamental issue behind all the secessions that took place, this ethnic intolerance, including our secession?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, my answer is probably already known. The reasons or the issues like ethnic intolerance and so on, or the reasons for the break-up of the SFRY fall outside the scope of my report. That's why I have not analysed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you are starting your analysis from the consequence, from the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if you prefer, you can go to the witness stand on your own. Do not argue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only want to point out to the witness, counting on his honesty, that his approach was wrong. I am asking him to consider whether it is true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You know the position of the witness already and his scope in relation to his report. Then it's for you later on to come up with a submission as to its credibility or the completeness. But do not argue with the witness and do not waste time, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know, Mr. Theunens, that before the war we accepted the fact that we did not have a continuity of territory and that Strategic Goal 2 was not indispensable, it only became so because of the war?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is Mr. Karadzic's interpretation. I have tried to explain in the report that what I called the take-over operations in Northern -- North-Eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina, which took place in April/May 1992, were actually part of the implementation of this second strategic goal, i.e., establishing a corridor between Krajina and Semberija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you establish that before we liberated the corridor, the other side took over power in Derventa, in Modrica, in Odzak, in Orasje, and Bosanski Brod, correct or not, in the former Province 3, according to the Vance-Owen Plan, the Posavina area? Do you know that they took over power before this happened and that they made it impossible for us to communicate?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in order to answer the question, I would like to refer to my report, footnotes 163 and 164 of Part 2, where, again, these are the minutes of the 16th Assembly session, and according to these minutes Mr. Karadzic explains, in relation to the second strategic goal, i.e., the corridor, that it is of "utmost strategic importance for the Serbian people because it integrates the Serbian lands." Furthermore, Mr. Karadzic states: "Krajina, Bosnian Krajina, Serbian Krajina, all the alliance of the Serbian states is not feasible if we fail to secure the corridor which will integrate us and give us unimpeded flow from one part of our state to another."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Hear him out, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I asked, Your Excellency. I'm asking whether they took the corridor before we did and made it impossible for us to travel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... No, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. So when Mr. Karadzic explains the strategic goal to the Assembly members, he doesn't refer to the activities of, call it, the other parties in relation to interrupting the corridor. He explains why the corridor is needed. And I think from the text, one can conclude that the main reason is to ensure the alliance of Serbian states and the unimpeded flow from "one part of our state to another."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you do not know whether it was triggered by war or not, because Mr. Karadzic didn't refer to it at his speech?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. My point is that if it was triggered by the others, then I would have expected Mr. Karadzic to provide another explanation to the Assembly members; i.e., that he would have explained to them that the corridor needs to be established because the others have interrupted it, as he's stating now. But based on the minutes, he does not explain it in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that neither of the "Krajinas" could survive for any other reason except that communication between them was interrupted and that this interruption occurred in the course of the war?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question, because the corridor connects -- I mean, the Posavina corridor connects Semberija with the two "Krajinas," I mean, Bosanska Krajina and the Krajina in Croatia. So Bosanska Krajina and the Krajina in Croatia are connected, except for what became the Bihac pocket. Now, whether or not they could survive without the corridor, I mean, according to what you said in -- on the 12th of May, 1992, indeed, the corridor was vital to ensure unimpeded flow from one part to the other. There was obviously also a political motivation to have the corridor; i.e., as you worded it, to -- otherwise, the alliance of the Serbian state was not feasible. And also when I discuss Operation Corridor, June, July, and November 1992, whereby elements of the RSK, I mean by that the RSK TO as well as the MUP, Ministry of the Interior, forces of the RSK, operate together under VRS command and control in the corridor to widen it, also there the vital nature of the corridor, as how the Serbs see it, is emphasised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It might be easier if I put the question like this: Before the corridor was broken through, were the "Krajinas" completely surrounded by the enemy, were they under siege?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, I can talk for the Krajina in Croatia, and I wouldn't define their status during the conflict in Croatia as being under siege.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. And do you recall that the third strategic goal was for the River Drina to be a soft border and that there should be no border restrictions between two worlds, not between two Serb countries, as you say in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, I would -- just for the sake of clarity, I use the term "Serbian state." A state is not necessarily the same as a country. And I can also refer -- again, it's in the text - I don't have to read it out - but under 2(c), the way how Mr. Karadzic presented that third goal to the Assembly members, whereby he also emphasizes the importance of that goal to damage the interests of the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. On footnote 163 has the six strategic goals, and then I quote from the minutes of the 16th Assembly session. And if you want, I can read it out. In relation to the third strategic goal, Mr. Karadzic states --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You read out part of it. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, do you have a 65 ter number for that? I think it's minutes of 16th session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is P00781.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this brought up on the screen? That's not it. T-1355 is the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we need that as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It would be P00956.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's first have the minutes, and then we'll move on to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it to come up, Mr. Theunens: Were these strategic goals on the agenda, and was a vote taken and a decision made?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, a decision is made, and it's disseminated through a document called "Decision --" I mean, this is in footnote 163. They are disseminated through a decision regarding the six strategic goals, number 02-130/92, signed by Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik, President of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us find that passage in the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the English -- I mean, when I -- the presentation by Mr. Karadzic of the strategic goals can be found on the English page ERN 0190-8523 to 8524.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But this document does not bear such ERN number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like a brief clarification. These are minutes, not the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you now, Mr. Theunens, is that neither on the agenda, nor in the decisions of the Assembly, is there any mention of the six strategic goals. That was information I provided on our negotiating positions, so it is not an official act of the Assembly because it can be found neither on the agenda, nor in the conclusions. If there's a hard copy, let someone show us that this was an official document which was adopted by the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, I just mentioned, I mean, in addition to the minutes, there is also the decision -- or the document called "The Decision on the Six Strategic Goals," signed by Mr. Krajisnik on the same date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. We'll come to that, and we'll see how it came about. But can we go through this page by page. 1, 2, 3 do not relate to this. Let's move on, let's go through the document. Next page, please. Here are the decisions adopted. Among these decisions, is there any decision on the adoption of the six strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this page, not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But, you know, when we go back to the previous page, I mean, these are decisions that need to be, if I understood it well, ratified or confirmed, the discussion of the strategic goals -- I mean, the presentation of the goals, and the discussion follows further in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see that a platform for negotiations with Yugoslavia is mentioned here and that I was asked to give my assessment of the political conditions and our negotiating position? Is there any discussion or adoption of a decision on the six strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on this page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is where the decisions -- the list of decisions ends with number 16. This is probably part of the transcript, and this is where I start to speak; right? "Ladies and gentlemen," that's the beginning of my speech, and it says here that this has happened to us before, only this time around it's different. The foundation of the HDZ is mentioned and the way this fact influences us. And now let's move on to the six strategic goals. [In English] Next page, please. [Interpretation] Do you agree that this is an expose by the president of the republic to the Assembly on his views, and the information he has, and what he has learned about the political conditions prevailing at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now go to the page on which I mention the six strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. You can see here that a conference is mentioned, and it says here at that conference, we achieved a great political success because the European Community has agreed on a tripartite Bosnia-Herzegovina, three constituent states, the relations among which will be stronger or firmer or looser. We were in favour of looser relations. We wanted these links to be very loose. The Croats wanted them to be even looser, but in Europe they wanted them to be stronger. That's not so important. What matters is that we received political endorsement of our will to have our own state in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was our legitimate right, and no one was denying it to us. And then I go on to say that after -- in the international recognition, the gentlemen from the Croatian and Muslim communities confessed that their participation in the conference was a purely tactical move, and they began to sabotage the conference in a brazen manner, unprecedented in diplomacy, and the European diplomats could not believe their eyes and ears. They could not understand that this was happening, and so on and so forth. Well, now can we move to where -- to the place where I speak of the six strategic goals. Do you agree, Mr. Theunens, that all this concerns the conference and the new order to be set up in Bosnia, this entire expose?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding, Your Honours, is that here Mr. Karadzic provides his interpretation of, indeed, the activities of the conference and -- the International Conference on the former Yugoslavia and related issues, and he explains his views on his interpretation to the Assembly members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is a document you are referring to in footnote 163?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. There are two documents in footnote 163. There are the minutes, and then I also included the document signed by Mr. Krajisnik that confirms the establishment of the six strategic goals and disseminates those goals or the information on it within the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we continue. May we go to the page where I speak of the strategic goals. What ERN number is that? Can somebody assist? Well, can we go through the document page by page, please. Let's go on. The strategic goals are not on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is about the division of the Ministry of the Interior. Do you know that at the conference, we got the right to have our own police?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I mentioned this morning, I did not analyse the activities of the conference. Now, if I had been asked to do so, then I would also have consulted not just the minutes to have Mr. Karadzic's interpretation of what the conference was doing or not doing, but I would also have used original documents issued by the conference or its members.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do we know what number it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second paragraph on this page, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-hah, look here. We did everything to prevent a war, and when war did break out, to have the war stop and for peace to be established, which would make a political solution possible. Every cease-fire was violated primarily by the Muslims in Sarajevo and the Croats in Posavina. That was the corridor. Do you see here that it was our standpoint that the war should not have broken out, that it should have been avoided, and once it did break out, on the 22nd of April I put forward the platform on the cessation of the conflict? Are you aware of that platform? It's of a military character. It's an original document of the protagonists whose conduct you were investigating.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't exactly recall which document includes the platform. But if Mr. Karadzic could show it to me, then I could review it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 1033, could we see that for a moment, please, and then we can return to this. We'll try to find the six strategic goals in the meantime. 65 ter 1033. It's a solitary document. On the 12th, we agreed on a cease-fire which wasn't honoured, and on the 22nd, I put forward the platform. This is the platform with which this Chamber is familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that I proposed an unconditional cease-fire, the immediate continuation of the conference, the drawing of maps within the framework of the conference which should be a priority, because that was our conclusion of the 12th of April with Ambassador Cutileiro? Then there's the public obligation of all sides in Bosnia: [In English] "... that the constitutional part of BH should not become a part of the neighbouring states and that no armed forces outside Bosnia and Herzegovina shall be called in or admitted into the territory of BH. "Public obligation that all the sides in BiH do not accept a 'fait accompli' policy, not the policy derived from Communist heritage, and that no advantage achieved by force should be justified. "Most immediate implementation of a new constitutional agreement with the international community warranties. "Initiation of demobilising process and transfer of JNA role within reasonable period." I think it was five years' period. [Interpretation] I think it was five years, the period in which the army should stay in order to prevent conflicts. Were you aware of this platform?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not seen this document before. As I said earlier, I had knowledge of the activities of the ICFY, the International Conference for the former Yugoslavia, from my professional activities prior to joining the OTP, but I had not seen the original of this document. Now, just to comment, if Mr. Karadzic, as the president of a party, can make a commitment or what appears to be a commitment in point 1 for an unconditional and immediate cease-fire in respect of the accord of the 12th of April - but I'm not familiar with the contents of the accord of the 12th of April - it would, from a military point of view, mean that as a party president he can, as least for the forces on his side, yes, make such a commitment that they would respect an unconditional cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is not the activity of the international community. It's my activity. I seek to tender this document. I believe that it should have been considered in your report; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I were to analyse the activities of the peace conference, for sure. Seeing it now, I think even within the scope, I would have included it, because as I mentioned now, I would see it as reflecting Mr. Karadzic's authority for the forces operating on the -- on the Bosnian Serb side, because he is in a position, looking at paragraph 1, to make a commitment for an unconditional and immediate cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted as Exhibit D -- you have objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D1587. But why was it translated in United Nations -- it is our paper, yes, it's our letterhead. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it was sent to them, Your Excellency, and that is why. The date is 22 April 1992. It was sent to them, and they translated it and forwarded it to the United Nations. Or, actually, this is the letterhead of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's not important. Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the previous document again, P956. Yes. Let us go forward in the document page by page and try to find the six strategic objectives. Page 7 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, consulting this document, did you read this platform or my speech I gave in the Assembly or did you just read the part about the six strategic objectives?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I read the entire document, whereby I would also use search terms to locate specific items in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the bottom of this page, I read: "The Serb side in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Presidency, the government, the National Security Council that we established, adopted the strategic priorities of the Serbian people," priorities, not objectives. It's on page 9 in English. The first strategic objective is the separation from the two other communities. Do you agree that this was one of the principles of the Lisbon Conference?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I answered the question already when I quoted from Mr. Krajisnik's -- excuse me, from Mr. Karadzic's explanation he provides to the Assembly members; that is, that he doesn't refer to the Lisbon Conference when he explains this goal to the Assembly members. And I have not analysed the documents of the Lisbon Conference, or the ICFY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he not talk about the conference earlier on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did earlier, Your Honours. But when he talks about the six strategic goals here, he doesn't -- when he talks about the first one, he doesn't refer to it. And I -- when reviewing the document, I have not found -- I mean, from reviewing the minutes, I have not found any reference between this first goal and his earlier explanations on the Lisbon Conference. And also if I were to make such a reference to the Lisbon Conference or the ICFY activities, I would have wanted to see the original documents of those conferences in order to see what was really proposed there and what was also, I think most importantly, the reaction of the other parties that were involved in the negotiations to any proposal like separation of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us see what we say about the second strategic goal. It continues to say if we were to stay together in the same state, they will continue to attack us. The second strategic goal is about the corridor, and it says it is something for which we may be forced to sacrifice something here and there, but this is of the utmost strategic importance. Do you understand, Mr. Theunens, that when I say that we will sacrifice something, it means that the Serbian side in the talks will have to give up some territories to get the corridor in return?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that may well be possible. But where we look at the conflict -- I mean, the conduct of the conflict between -- during the existence of the VRS, May 1992 until the Dayton Agreement, and the cease-fire just prior to that, say November 1995, then we see that keeping the corridor open was a priority for the VRS which required them to limit the number of forces in other areas in order to free sufficient forces and equipment, of course, in order to keep the corridor open, because the corridor was the life-line with Serbia. And so from a military point of view, sacrificing something here and there is related to the fact that the number of troops in here and there, in other areas, has to be reduced or limited because these troops are needed in the corridor, and these troops and these means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Theunens, how you arrive at your conclusions by means of analogies. But this is quite explicit. Do you know that I accepted the Vance-Owen Plan according to which the corridor was not ours and that we only needed the corridor during the war and if there should be war, but it isn't required in peace? Do you know that Province 3 -- or, rather, do you know to who Province 3 was supposed to go, and do you know that I initialled that on the 1st of May, 1993, in Athens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm familiar with the Vance-Owen Plan from my activities prior to joining the OTP, but I also remember that, actually, the Bosnian Serbs rejected the map included in the Vance-Owen Plan on the basis, I think, of a vote by the Assembly members during a meeting held in Pale which was also attended by the president of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Milosevic, and during which General Mladic explained which territorial concessions the Bosnian Serbs would have to make if they accepted the Vance-Owen Plan. So I think we should look at these various aspects of the negotiations and phases of the negotiations together, and the end result was that the Bosnian Serbs rejected the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the question was whether you know about Province 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would have to see the map. I don't remember which province was Province 3. Vance-Owen spoke about ten provinces, and there would also be, I think, an international statute for Sarajevo, but I don't recall the exact map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that I accepted - and I am standing trial here - not the Serbian people, and the Assembly could not decide, but put it -- put the question in a referendum, but the Serbian people refused, whereas I am standing trial here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it's correct that it was the Serbian people who refused in the referendum. I didn't recall it exactly. I mean the Bosnian Serb people, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at Strategic Goal 3: "The third strategic goal is to establish a corridor in the Drina Valley, that is, the elimination of the Drina as a border between two worlds." Does this say "border between Serbian states" or "border between two worlds"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There it says, "Elimination of the Drina as a border between two worlds."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree or do you know that the Drina was the border between the West Roman Empire and the East Roman Empire and that it continues to be the point of contact between East and West, and now also includes Islam? Is that the meaning of this phrase "border between two worlds," that is, border between East and West, and we wanted to eliminate this border?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be an explanation. But, I mean, when you continue to read there, you state: "We are on both sides of the Drina, and our strategic interest and our living space are there." When you look at the map and you look at which people or which entities or states exist on both sides of the Drina, well, on the eastern side you had the Republic of Serbia, and on the western side there were, among others, Bosnian Serbs living there. So my conclusion was that the "we" refers to the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that St. Sava, a Serbian prince and monk in the 13th century, said that, We are the West to the East and the East to the West, and that we should be the bridge between the East and the West? When I say that, it's clear to any Serb, but you may not understand because you don't know about St. Sava. But we consider ourselves a bridge between East and West. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am generally familiar with St. Sava, but in my interpretation or my analysis, the statements of St. Sava are not relevant in this context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So both subjects in the second and third sentences are identical, "we"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When we use the term "we," my interpretation is that it talks about the Serbian people or the Serbs, whereby they don't make a distinction between Serbs living in Croatia, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or in Serbia, or in Montenegro, even.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, because we're the same people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But look at this. We say here: "We now see a possibility for some Muslim municipalities to be set up along the Drina as enclaves ..." The "we" here refers to the leadership of the RS, and I'm talking about the outcome of the conference. And I say that there will be Muslim municipalities along the Drina. How does that compare to your conclusions that we attacked Srebrenica because we didn't want any enclaves, although we were always for the Muslims having their territories in the Drina area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the conclusion that - I'm quoting now from the question from Mr. Karadzic - that "We attacked Srebrenica because we didn't want any enclaves," I didn't draw that conclusion myself. We discussed the Directive 6 that was signed by Mr. Karadzic, or it may even be Directive 7 - I'm confused now - but, anyway, Directive 6 or Directive 7 which have been admitted into evidence, they expressed the goals set by Mr. Karadzic -- I mean, the military goals set by Mr. Karadzic as to the future of these enclaves and the people living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And I say, Mr. Theunens, that we conducted the operation of the separation of Zepa and Srebrenica, and not to take them over, because they were killing us daily. And you see that the third strategic goal has nothing to do with the elimination of the enclaves, because our view was that they could have enclaves in the Drina area. Doesn't this say so, and don't you know that in nearly all plans, we accepted that part of the Drina area belonged to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But, Your Honour, we should read the whole paragraph. I mean, Mr. Karadzic even states, okay, that he sees the possibility -- or the RS leadership, as he calls it, sees the possibility for some Muslim municipalities to be set up along the Drina as enclaves in order for them to achieve their rights, but that belt along the Drina must basically belong to Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina. And he continues to explain -- well, maybe they tolerate initially the existence of these enclaves, but there is a clear agenda between -- behind tolerating these enclaves. And that can also be seen by the next sentence -- I mean, the last three lines of that paragraph.
