utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where does it say at the beginning? It says here: "... in order for them to achieve their rights, but that belt along the Drina must basically belong to Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina. As much as it is strategically useful for us in a positive way, it helps us by damaging the interests of our enemy in establishing a corridor which would connect them to the Muslim international ..." Do you think that Islamic fundamentalism should have been our friend and that we didn't have the right to prevent the advance of Muslim fundamentalism into our country? I don't care about Europe. Let Europe take care of itself.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this issue, I mean the issue of "Islamic fundamentalism" falls outside the scope of my report. And when I discuss the strategic goals, I don't express any judgement as to whether they were good, or bad, or anything. I just factually quote them. And then by analysing the documentation that I reviewed, I came to the conclusion that there was a consistency between the strategic goals, as the highest level of political direction to the military, on one hand, and, on the other hand, the operations conducted by the VRS between its creation in May 1992 until the cease-fire agreement of the fall 1995. And just I would like to correct my previous answer, when I spoke -- when I was confusing -- confounding Directive 6 and 7. It should be Directive 7, and it's footnote 371 in Part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll come to that. Could we see 1D3926 and see what Alija Izetbegovic's son, Bakir, said at his inaugural speech upon -- on the occasion of his election to the Dayton Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which had three members. That is connected with the third strategic goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we just hear what the relevance of that is, because it's really something that is from this year or last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But he says it's related to the third strategic goal. I cannot make that assessment until I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, Mr. Izetbegovic, in 2010, November 2010, repeats that Bosnia is a contact point between worlds. That's what matters to me. I just have to find the line. It's in paragraph 4. Actually, 3. Yes: "The idea of Bosnia-Herzegovina obviously transcends its geographical size, its borders. This is the contact point between borders. This is a knot where not only Bosnian and Herzegovinian but global interests are tied or untied." Actually, it's not "interests," it's "relations." Do you see, Mr. Theunens, that the logic of the Muslim leader and the Serbian leader is the same with regard to worlds being in contact with each other in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now it's time for you to explain the relevance of this document, to Strategic Goal 3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I speak about transcending borders between two worlds, not between Serbs and Strategic Goal 3, because the River Drina was also called the border between two worlds. It was the border between two Roman empires. And this idea is something that is very present in our minds, and an analyst shouldn't make a mistake with regard to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How is this passage related to that borders between the two worlds? I have difficulty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not saying that the Drina should be the border between two Serbian states, but I am speaking about the border between two worlds, and that's what Mr. Izetbegovic also says. We're speaking about something global, something spiritual here, not states.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. I'm asking -- maybe asking about your case. Your case is that the Drina used to be the border between the two worlds, East and West, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And concerning the third strategic goal, I say that we should do something so that the Drina no longer be the border between two worlds. I'm not referring to two Serbian states, which has been attributed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber does not see any relevance of what Mr. Izetbegovic's son is talking about after so many years. Move on to your document -- move on to your next document, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please view the video, then, and let us see what I said about the third strategic objective in a TV interview in 1993. I think that there can be no confusion. I think that is the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The last question and we have to finish this show of ours. Now, when will the borders become softer and --" "Mr. Karadzic: It seems that the Muslim leadership, as they --"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have given them the Serbian transcript, and we are going to ask for them to interpret while they hear what is being said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It is very fast, it is very hard to follow it except from the text.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "They have to report to their units." "Reporter: The last question of the viewers and now we have to finish this programme. When will the borders between Serbia and Republika Srpska become softer, and does the world know that there is no such border between Croatia and --" The interpreter did not hear the rest. "What they meant was --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's go back and repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The last question of the viewers, and now we have to finish this programme of ours. When will the borders between Serbia and Republika Srpska become softer, and does the world know that there are no such borders between Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina?" "Karadzic: It seems to me that as the Muslim leadership put forth these requests for the central government to guard the borders, primarily meant the border between Herzegovina and Croatia, which does exist and where there are no restrictions, rather, the border on the Drina River. We will never allow that. That is one of the strategic objectives that we have established at our Assembly. We are never going to allow a border to pass through Serb areas and to be a real border with restrictions, although that is the way it was for a while, because overall economic relations were such that for a while it had to be that way. Now it is going to be quite different. Finally, whichever way it is resolved, Serb areas in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina will have great freedom in economic and any other links with whomever they wish. That is the way it is according to the Lisbon paper, and according to these papers, and also in --" Interpreter's note: No, the interpretation has not finished. It was very fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters -- please, we have to repeat. You overlapped with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "That is the way it is in accordance with the Lisbon paper and according to these papers, rather, everything that is a trend in Europe currently. Those are the rights enjoyed by Germans and French, that is, that is the right that Alsace and Lorraine enjoy, that is the right the Serbs have to have on both sides of the Drina River."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's got to be more. That is a European trend, and then I said that Maastricht -- or, rather, soft borders in Europe would be established. Could it all be read out?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is the end of the transcript that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we play it again, only the last part.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Disabled persons who fought and --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "We are never going to allow a border going through Serb areas become a true border, although it was that way for a while, because overall economic relations were such that it had to be that way for a while. Now it is going to be quite different. Finally, no matter how it is resolved, Serb areas in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina are going to enjoy great freedom, in terms of economic and any other links, with whoever they wish. That is the way it is according to the Lisbon paper, and according to these papers, and in accordance with what the trend is currently in Europe. Those are the rights enjoyed by the Germans and the French. Those are the rights that are enjoyed by Alsace and Lorraine. These rights have to be enjoyed by Serbs on both sides of the Drina River."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that has been interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Alsace and Lorraine, the Germans and French. Do you understand now that the third strategic objective was perceived as a border without restrictions, a soft border like the one that will exist in Europe, not the unification of two Serb lands?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't use the term "unification of Serb lands." I just talk about eliminating the Drina as a border, and then I added myself "separating Serbian states," because that's my interpretation of the second sentence in this paragraph discussing the third strategic goal; that is, when Mr. Karadzic says to the Assembly members: "We are on both sides of the Drina, and our strategic interest and our living space are there." And my impression is also from the interview we heard, that in the beginning he also emphasizes the fact that a border between the Serbs on both sides of the Drina is unacceptable for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And in this interview, at the end, Mr. Karadzic said, These rights have to be enjoyed by Serbs on both sides of the Drina River, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the 65 ter number of this, Mr. Karadzic? That will be sorted out later. I take it there's no position --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3930, 1D3930.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1588, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go back to the previous document, that transcript from the Assembly. Let us look at the fourth, fifth and sixth strategic objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that the first map gave us a border on the Una, Sava, Drina, in part, and partly on the Neretva River, the Cutileiro map and all other maps, and today we are on Drina, Una, Sava and the upper part of the Neretva River, that is what Dayton recognised for us --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I haven't analysed these maps for my report, but if my views would be requested, I would like to see the maps and then compare the maps. I see that here in the document reference is made to a working map, which suggests to me it's not the final map, so we also have to consider the different versions of the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But, Mr. Theunens, in every map we were on the Una, Sava, Drina, Neretva, on each and every map. Did you know that, that this was no new strategic objective; rather, it was a platform for further negotiations, that we shall continue to seek that because that is what had been offered to us and that is what we got? There is no dispute there.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I remember the different maps that were proposed throughout the conflict during the various attempts the international community made to try to find a peaceful solution to the conflict; the Cutileiro, Vance-Owen, Owen-Stoltenberg -- Owen-Stoltenberg, sorry, Contact Group, and at the end, the Dayton map. Now, it's a matter of interpretation. There may have been areas under Serb control that bordered on these -- on the rivers Mr. Karadzic has identified, but I can say, without having the maps in front of me, that they are all quite different; in particular, in relation to the number of entities as well as the percentage of territory that would be given to the -- to the different entities or parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in the Cutileiro proposal before the war, were Serbs also given the Una as a natural boundary?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember -- I don't recall the exact map or the final map in the Cutileiro proposal, so I cannot answer the question. And, again, it falls outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But you are actually looking at the reasons for the activity of Republika Srpska. You are justifying that by the strategic objectives that were political ones and basically agreed upon before the war. Therefore, they were a very important element in your report. They were taken as a reason for the activity of the Army of Republika Srpska. And I am telling you that we never denied the existence of Muslim municipalities in Podrinje, in the Drina River Valley. Do you know that President Milosevic said in Dayton, in agreement with me, that one could discuss the return of Zepa and Srebrenica to the Muslims? If you look at these transcripts, they're not accessible to us, but that was said, with my consent. It was not our objective for them not to exist there, but not to allow them to kill us. And even in Dayton, we allowed for the possibility of their having their own municipality there.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can only answer by referring again to the directive for further operations number 7, which is footnote 370, and, more specifically, footnote 371 in Part 2 of the report, which establishes the mission or the task of the VRS Drina Corps, just recalling that this directive is signed by Mr. Karadzic, as the supreme commander, where, I start to quote: "The VRS --"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll deal with that tomorrow. Please, can we have the next page? Can we look at the fifth strategic objective?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a moment. Is your question no or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Answer, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question was whether in Dayton, Mr. Karadzic and Milosevic allowed for the possibility of Muslims having their own municipality there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably they did, in the sense that an agreement was concluded and now there is a Muslim -- I mean, after Dayton, a Muslim or Bosniak municipality was established in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "We established," sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at the fifth strategic objective now. Do you know that throughout the negotiations, our position was for the city not to be divided, and for Bosnia not to be divided, but rather to have an administrative reorganisation? Instead of ten mixed municipalities, it would be ten ethnically-determined municipalities, like in Brussels. That's the example that we gave, not Beirut, not Nicosia, but Brussels. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with, again, what the Bosnian Serbs or Mr. Karadzic proposed during the negotiations or the peace talks of ICFY. I mean, I don't remember the details. But I think the text here on his explanation he gives to the delegates is quite clear. It is that as long as -- he says "Alija," which refers to Izetbegovic, "does not have a state, while we have a part of Sarajevo," and I think that's important to understand in the context of assessing the importance of the fifth strategic goal and its relevance for Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But do you know - you should know, really - that this is not a new objective that was placed on the 9th of May, this is an objective that had been discussed, and there was two variants. One was for Sarajevo to be extraterritorial, a condominium of all three ethnic communities, for a while under UN administration, and the second variant was that if there is no war, that existing municipalities should only be reorganised, that they should be Serb, Croat, or Muslim municipalities; yes or no? If you didn't know about it, no problem.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't -- I'm not familiar with what Mr. Karadzic is saying now. Now, it may well have been his point of view at the time. In any event, we can also see what is happening on the ground in Sarajevo already prior to the announcement of the sixth strategic goal, when we discuss -- I mean, in the section on Sarajevo in my report on -- starting with footnote 657 until footnote 666, where I discuss activities of Bosnian Serb forces, including crisis staffs in various municipalities in Sarajevo prior to -- or in April and May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it your position that the Serbs held Sarajevo under siege?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is a different question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could it be answered with a yes-or-no answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I cannot answer it as a yes-or-no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I see. I see. Okay, proceed, proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- because I don't have an exact recollection of what is written in the documents of Sarajevo Romanija Corps. I mean, if I would express myself here as to whether it was under siege or not under siege, I have not analysed the status of Sarajevo during the conflict. I could understand that question if that terminology would be used in one of the, call it, directives or other command documents, or other military documents from the VRS, if they would use the word "siege," and then I would say, Look, the city was under siege because of this and this document. So I can conduct that search after court, but otherwise, I mean, I have not assessed or analysed the status of Sarajevo between May 1992 and October 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the sixth strategic objective, do you know that Mr. Tudjman, Mr. Izetbegovic and I had reached an agreement that Bosnia-Herzegovina relinquishes its rights in Neum and the Serbs and Muslims -- Serbs and Croats, rather, get access to the sea, also along the border with Montenegro, and that that was even in the draft of the third agreement, the Owen-Stoltenberg agreement, and our access to the sea was actually depicted there? Yes or no. You do know or you don't know, that's it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and I believe it was also known as the "Invincible" Agreement or Negotiations because these talks took place on the British Navy ship HMS Invincible at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you say whether we ever tried to achieve that sixth strategic objective by military means?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot answer the question from the top of my head. I would first look at the directives and see whether there are any instructions in these nine directives for the VRS to conduct such operations. Now, I do remember that -- again from my activities outside of the OTP, that no such military operations took place, except for the fact that the VRS occasionally, and that was usually at the beginning of the touristic season, would carry out some symbolic artillery shelling of the wider hinterland of Dubrovnik, but -- and again that happened, for example, when I was serving in UNPROFOR. We did not believe that the aim of the Bosnian Serbs was to force an access to the sea. It was more to harass the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, now you've given me some homework to clarify the matter tomorrow, because that was not true. It was not our interest to quarrel with the Croats. We had a good life with them during the war. We traded with them, and my army would not have survived, I would not have survived, without this trade with the Croats. Did you know that, because Yugoslavia, as you said, in August 1994 imposed sanctions on Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the question covers several aspects. Relations between the Bosnian Serbs and the Bosnian Croats and Croats are not covered in my report, but I know, from my work prior to joining the OTP, that, in particular on the local level, for example, in the area of Kiseljak, and also in other areas, there were good relations between the Bosnian Croats and the Bosnian Serbs. This changed over time, like after the conclusion of the Federation Agreement in February 1994. On the other hand, there were, indeed, sanctions imposed by the president of the Republic of Serbia against the Bosnian Serbs in August 1994 to punish them for their refusal of accepting the Contact Group Plan. But from the documents discussed in the section on relations between the VJ and the VRS, these sanctions did not interrupt the assistance provided by the VJ to the VRS. And that was also highlighted, for example, when we discussed SDC minutes - SDC of the FRY - minutes during the examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Theunens, the problem is that you are expanding this story and you're saying that this army, whose civilian chief I was, shelled the hinterland of Dubrovnik to harm tourism, and that is to my detriment and it's not true. And I said that we had a good life with the Croats. They gave us oil. We gave them electricity with Boban. I pacified huge parts of the front-line already on the 5th of May in Graz, but you probably don't know about any of this. All right, let us cover a few topics before we stop for the day. Yesterday, on page 7, line 21, up until line 25 on page 8, you were asked whether I could have ordered an investigation, and then a document was put to you in which a commission had been established to investigate what happened in Banja Luka in September 1993; that is to say, page 7, line 21, until page 8, line 25. Mr. Theunens, is this a criminal investigation or is it a parliamentary investigation of a political nature?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, one document I quote in relation to that talks about an investigation commission. It doesn't use the expression "criminal" nor "parliamentary." I'm just locating now whether I have another document that deals with these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Among those names, do you find any criminal lawyers, any lawyers in general, any judges, or are these people parliamentarians, representatives of the Main Staff, the head of my military office? In a word, you were asked whether I, as supreme commander, had the ability to order investigations, and what was shown to you was that example. And I am telling you that that is an example of a parliamentary investigation, not a criminal investigation, because a president cannot order judiciary organs to carry out an investigation. The president can only ask for their views, but cannot order an investigation to take place. Have you found a single example of the president interfering with the work of the judiciary?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have -- I haven't seen a document where Mr. Karadzic issues orders to conduct an investigation to the civilian judiciary. However, in footnote 1029, page 295 of the second part of the report, Mr. Karadzic, on the 15th of March, 1995, issues a direct instruction to General Tolimir, and now I quote, to order the security organs of the VRS to take -- okay, quotation, "appropriate measures," against the Command of the 3rd Battalion in Olovo. And according to the document, Mr. Karadzic has information that the command of the battalion has committed several criminal offences in relation to commercial crime. So I agree, it's not ordering an investigation, but it's ordering those who can conduct an investigation in such matters, i.e., the security organs, to then take appropriate measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The footnote number again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1029, Your Honours, in Part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's probably different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I have a different version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You probably came across documents where I am urging for speedier trials, asking that criminals not be released, and so on. Have you ever found any example of any interference of mine with the prosecution or with the judiciary? Tolimir is part of the prosecution process, and I'm asking him to do something. Did you find any example of my interfering in somebody else's work, not taking into account the fact that I urged for speedier processes, because I wasn't really interfering with the merits of the cases?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I have not seen such examples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll rise for today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to put one more question, if we have time for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked, on page 64, line 20, until page -- the next page about the Documentation Centre -- the Investigation and Documentation Centre concerning war crimes against non-Serbs: [In English] "... Non-Serbs ... describe your report... we did not need --" [Interpretation] Documentation Centre concerning war crimes against non-Serbs. This Documentation Centre, is it part of a criminal investigation process or does it have to do with archives and documentation? It is page 16 in English. Your report, actually, page 16 in English. So this is a documentation centre for collecting information from the territory that our investigation organs do not have access to. Is this a documentation centre or is it an investigation centre, since it was headed by Mr. Toholj, who is a well-known writer, and there are no judges or lawyers in that body? In other words, can this replace criminal processes, and does this annul in any way criminal processes in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Documentation Centre, we also saw an order by Colonel Lugonja that was discussed in the examination. Lugonja, chief of the security organs in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, concerned crimes committed against Serbs, not non-Serbs. And I agree with Mr. Karadzic. These -- I mean, the motives or the reasons behind the establishment of these centres is not clear or the orders to collect this evidence, I mean the order by Lugonja. But from the information that's available, it does not allow to conclude that it replaces the criminal process or the judicial process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to rise immediately. 9.00, tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
